blocks.text: The horn blew and the Black Brothers gathered as they had gathered for hundreds of years. It was a feeble call, that horn, there on those hard Steppes. The wind tore the note as lions tear a calf, twisting it, tossing it aloft until naught but an echo remained.

blocks.text: The LT climbed atop one of the few remaining wagons. He waited, quietly, gaze downward, as was his way. Brothers thronged like school children awaiting their noontide story. Some sat, others crouched. A few stretched out on the sands, hands cupped behind their heads, staring at the LT and the splash of diamonds in the night sky serving as his backdrop. Several murmurs, a belch or two, a laugh, then silence. Save for the wind – always the wind, these past four years.

Two nights in the city, tops, and then you’re to heel-toe it back. If you ain’t back in five, we’re moving on without you.” Bigby shared a look with the group of men. “And we’ll do it, lads. We can’t afford to linger, and we’re in no shape to mount no rescue operation.”

entries.author: The_Frostrune
entries.body: Gallows shifts the wad of blackroot to his other cheek.  "Sarge, do we know if this city up ahead is on this side of the river or the far side?  Walled or open?"

entries.author: smalls
entries.body: "Far side. Single bridge. Piece of shit, from what they say, like to crumble into the water the next bad look it gets. No way we're getting Tadpole across while he's conscious. "

entries.author: smalls
entries.body: "City both walled and not. Guess there's a huge portion of slums spilling out from the walled section."

entries.author: The_Frostrune
entries.body:
Gallows pauses for a bit while he seems to be working through something in his head.  

“So this bridge is in bad shape, like weak and rickety?   Too weak for cavalry?  Seems like the city don’t expect much in the way of travelers from this direction ?”  He eyes the Sergeant looking for a nod.  

Seeing nothing but Bigby’s impatient scowl through his bushy brows he continues to spell out his logic. “mayhap those camel riding scouts ain’t from the city?  Bandits too weak to prey on a force our size?  Maybe the city doesn’t know we’re coming…. yet?”

entries.author: smalls
entries.body:
Bigby shrugs. "Logic seems to work. I couldn't say, cause I ain't eyed it myself. Wait one. "

The big bellied Sergeant sticks his head outside his tent and bellows for Awkward and Barnacle. After a bit, the two brothers join you. Bigby says, "Tell Gallows and the boys what you saw. "

Awkward nods and screws up his face in serious thought. "Well, we was just up in the ridge. Staying below the horizon. So we couldn't see much.  Watched the city while the sun..."

Here Awkward pauses, as his name would suggest. Barnacle takes up the report: "... Set. Mayhap an hour all told. Bridge is stone. Real thin. Like wide enough for one man, maybe. Not sure a horse or camel could do it, to tell it true. Would have to be a pretty damned trained mount, and a damned good rider. It's more like-"

Awkward jumps in, "-an archway than a bridge. Water brown as latrine slurry. No telling how deep or how fast. 

"The city seems like two cities to be honest, right on the other side. River's maybe three hundred paces wide there at the bridge. Anyway, two cities. Actually, three cities because..."

Barnacle: "... There's clearly one old city. Ruins mainly I guess. Big stone columns and temples and steps and fancy stuff. Then there's a city of tents a little huts and what not, clustered around those ruins like mushrooms at the base of a big, mature forest. And then-"

Awkward: "-there's a third city. Big sprawl of canvas and leather shanties. Damn big. We seen the like before, back east. I could almost imagine the smell even up on the ridge."

entries.author: TheBit
entries.body:
Prancer takes one of the gold coins from his purse, studies it casually, and then starts turning it back and forth over his knuckles at an impressive pace.

“Since we only have two days, I think it imperative we stay in the city the first night. I would hate to walk in looking as we do, so obviously foreign to this region. It would at least be nice to pass as someone from this side of the Steppes.”

Prancer pauses a moment to study everyone’s faces, then continues. “Do we think we can parlay with one of these camel riders? We may, perhaps, glean some of the customs of the land, the dialect, maybe even figure out a way to pick up some clothes that aren’t an immediate giveaway that we aren’t from around here. I find most folks aren’t amenable to gossiping with strangers in the first place, let alone a foreign stranger.”

“I think our best chance is to spread out when we get there and, while I know this is likely difficult for some of you, try not to pick a fight. Traveling over these steppes, for as long as we have, has no doubt made some of our social graces a bit rusty. I contend we will be best served if we can spend our two days in this city without making any impression at all.”

entries.author: The_Frostrune
entries.body: “Nice work boys!  Camel jockeys definitely not from city. Snakes can track ‘um but probably couldn’t keep up.  Not our mission but Maybe Cap can signal ‘um next time they show?”

entries.author: The_Frostrune
entries.body: He stands and moves a few paces to clap Prancer on the back “Not sure any of us had social graces to forget.”

entries.author: smalls
entries.body: Sergeant Mercy enters the chat/tent. He nods to Bigby, frowns at Awkward, then eyes each of you in turn. "I know the Old Man's told you, as I'm sure Sergeant Bigby and everyone else has, the whole 'no trouble' warning. 'Don't get in no trouble.' 'Don't stir up no trouble.'" He spits. "That's fine and mayhap that's even smart. I won't go second guessing the Cap.  But I know this, sure as shit, you boys are repping the Company down there. Ain't no one gonna sign a good contract over to fancy lads and pussyfolk. So if trouble happens to find *you* then remember we got all that shit Croaker reads about to uphold. If I find out any of you cunts lay down and show your backside,...well, we is gonna do the dance should you make it back. And you won't like that none."

entries.author: TheBit
entries.body:
"Do not worry Sergeant, if trouble finds us, we will leave no doubt we are not to be trifled with. Given the mission, though, we should at least try to approach it with some tact. I would submit that when we leave the city, no one should have any idea who we are. Ideally, at least as far as the city-folk are concerned, we are not 'representing the Black' at all."

Prancer looks around the room at the  Brothers assembled, ponders a moment, drops his head and shakes it as the corners of his mouth curl up into the slightest of smiles.  He then looks up at Sergeant Mercy. "After some consideration, I suspect trouble may very well find us after all."

entries.author: Fitz
entries.body: "Hold up. I'm confused."  This is not a new adjective for Bumble.  "Prancer, how we gonna be renowned enough to snag a contract if we are so forgettable?  Don't we gotta do something memorable down there to get picked up?  How bout we figure out the factions and try to do something to impress the one seems most likely to want our services? Even if that thing might get us in a scrape or two."

entries.author: Fitz
entries.body:
Bumble continues speaking low and slow.  "Sarges, if the Black's gonna prance around down there for a couple days..." He glances at Prancer with a twinkle in his eye.   "You sure you want me in there? I ain't the best at...uh...talking... or thinking. Or reading the mood.  Or sayin' the right thing." His pace and volume are going up as he continues. "Come to think of it, I'm not really good at anything but smashing shit!"  

Bigby stands and shouts at Bumble who is also now standing. "Secure that shit now!"

Bumble's eyes burn with fury as he grinds his teeth briefly.  He nods once and sits. "Sorry, boys."

Bigby nods once, the outburst forgotten. "You'll go down there, ya big piece of meat, and you'll support your brothers as they collect intel. I know you ain't the thinker or the diplomat, dipshit.  But you're a dab hand at smashing shit as you said, and the boys may need that. Besides. You said it yourself, dumbass. You're there for the scrape that might happen."

Bumble squints.  "Oh. Right."

entries.author: Kartoonstew
entries.body:
Tulip chuckles to himself, concealing it poorly.

"Something funny, Tulip?", Bigby says sternly.

"No sir, well — yessir." Tulip scratched the back of his neck. "Jes' finking me an' ol' Smooth Brain oughta maybe be kept apart when it comes to the sort o' fings what call for, whassat fing Prancer said, tact? anything wiv more'n two syllables an' we're already in trouble, the pair of us." He he looked around, gathering himself a bit. 

"Do me best to keep me 'ead down an' me mouf shut. Ain't easy after wha' we been frough, mind. Charm's a bit rusty."
He let that sit a beat, then his brow creased.
"Right, anyway, these camel riders. Tha's all well an' good but it gives us fuck all out 'ere, duddunit? Anyone actually clapped eyes on the people in the city? Not them them riders, but the city proper. 'Cause we're goin' in blind as bats an' I'd rather know if they're like to spit on us or stick a blade in us before we go smilin' frough the gates."

entries.author: Catfish
entries.body:
Going with Twitch for now until we settle on a nickname...

"Blind ain't so bad," Twitch blurted out, the words tumbling over each other, rapid-fire, awkwardly avoiding eye contact. "Blind means they ain't seen us neither, not if we do it right. Slums is slums. Folks in a sprawl like that... they're hungry, and either they're scared or they're lookin' to cut a purse. Ain't gotta clap eyes on 'em to know 'at much."

He shifts his weight entirely, scratching at the heavy stubble on his jaw.

"Fancy lad's right," Twitch says, jerking his chin toward Prancer. "We don't go strollin' through the old ruins first. And big man," his eyes flick to Bumble, "we don't smash nuffin' unless we got a clear way back across that skinny bridge. Unless we like getting fucked."

Prancer makes a look that says he likes getting fucked very much. Twitch ignores him.

He leans forward slightly, accent thickening into the harsh, clipped tones of a low-born runner. "We go when the market's thickest, or we go in the pitch. I can slip over first. Find the shadows. Eyes open, mouf shut. We find out who runs the gutters. Them always knows what the high-castle bosses are doin', 'cause they the ones always cleanin' up their shite."

entries.author: smalls
entries.body: Mercy eyes Twitch like a man might eye another man who claims to be a grapefruit. "I hear you boys - you just now, Twitch, and Prancing Lad earlier - talking 'bout spreading and splitting. Before you all get ungovernably cunty just remember the Old Man is sending some muscle with ya and if that muscle ain't there to pull the knob out yer ass, well, t'aint much good for ye, is it?"

entries.author: Kartoonstew
entries.body: "splittin seems unwise, innit?"

entries.author: smalls
entries.body: Bigby leans back. "Splittin's for pussy, firewood, and bananas." He pulls out a pipe and pretends to smoke it, given the BC has been without tobacco or its like for nearly a year. "That being said, I'm sure the LT named his names for a reason and part o' that, I'll allow - though it gives me gut some flutterin' - may be to let the sneaky sneaks sneak. At least a mite bit."

entries.author: Kartoonstew
entries.body: "aye! let the sneaks sneak, fair nuff". Tulip's eyes hang on the obviously empty pipe for a beat.

entries.author: The_Frostrune
entries.body:
“Whole lot of guesses and assumptions at this point.  We’re gonna have to improvise .   First problem is getting across the River.”

“Won’t know til we see it but bridge sounds crazy exposed.  I’d prefer we scout up or down River and hopefully find a boat, ferry, or ford.  We gotta get the company across at some point. The Old Man is gonna want to know that info anyway.”

entries.author: The_Frostrune
entries.body:
“As for the whole blend in thing… I say fuck it.   These soft city boys see outlanders that survived the wastes…. they’re gonna rightly guess we gotta be pretty bad ass.”

“I ain’t saying we swagger in Dicks swinging, but we ain’t fooling anyone.  Prancer and Grimace might be able talk the talk but our accents and obvious questions are going to scream we aren’t from around here”

entries.author: Kartoonstew
entries.body: "right right, we ain't blendin in fer nuffin methinks. We is what we is and we aint what we aint. But yer right, Gallows, will keep me dick in me pants. well, at least ain't swingin er round, like ye say. Any uh you cunts able to scout the river?"

entries.author: TheBit
entries.body: "So...if we're not trying to blend in, then why are we not just walking across the bridge?  I understand the potential benefit of entering unseen, but it doesn't sound like we're particularly interested in taking advantage of them. Do we anticipate a rain of arrows if we simply try to walk into town?"

entries.author: Kartoonstew
entries.body: "I don' see how we blend in. but 'ssumin they ain't friendly, and we dunno, bridge is risky methinks"

entries.author: TheBit
entries.body: "Why are we assuming they aren't friendly, exactly? We're a likable lot, I think."

entries.author: smalls
entries.body: Bigby pretends to blow a smoke ring. "'Don't know about whether you're likeable or not. I have my guess. But blendin' in will be tough, given most of the swinging Richards around here are the color of my soiled underpants. That's asumming, I s'pose, that the city folk look like them camel humpers we've seen. Could be wrong."

entries.author: The_Frostrune
entries.body: Gallows looks at Prancer and shrugs.  “Seems to me walking across that bridge is exactly like swaggering in, cocks swinging.   Your mom was pretty impressed but I’m not sure how it will go over with the locals.”

entries.author: TheBit
entries.body: "Yes, the audacity to just walk into a city by the most convenient means. I see what you mean."

entries.author: Fitz
entries.body: Bumble gives an uncharacteristic smirk at that comment from Prancer. His smiles are almost always reserved for an enemy combatant...or when he's bleeding freely.

entries.author: Fitz
entries.body: "I know I'm not The Thinker here, but I'm smelling the strong scent of Over Think here. I'm with Prancer.  We just walk across the bridge and enter the town. If we get shot at or attacked...well... seems maybe this ain't the place to land a contract then, eh?"

entries.author: The_Frostrune
entries.body: Gallows' eyes narrow a bit, rolls the blackroot around in his cheek but chooses to hold his peace.

entries.author: BGM
entries.body: Grimace sighs, appears somewhat annoyed (nothing new), “So, we’re walking in then? Across the bridge?”

entries.author: Fitz
entries.body: "Well I ain't in charge but seems like the way, especially if we're trying to remain neutral and not piss anyone off right off."

entries.author: BGM
entries.body:
“Unless I missed something, sneaky is an option? I have no doubts about our Sneaks capabilities, but if you’re caught; you’re fucked, and we can’t help you because then the mission is over.”

“If we disguise ourselves and we blow it somehow, that makes us look bad.”

“If we just walk in, looking like ‘we can handle ourselves’ as it was put… across the rickety stone ‘bridge’, as if we have a reason to be here… then we just ‘ask’ for information.”

“If it goes south then we have options.  If the numbers favor us, we fight.  If they are even, we negotiate. If we are outmatched, then we pull back across the bridge. It’s a choke point and numbers mean nothing. We fight or continue our retreat.”

entries.author: The_Frostrune
entries.body: Gallows shakes his head and grumbles under his breath, *"300 yd single-file approach ain't no retreat.  We either get in or we get dead.  Guess the Gods want a good laugh before they send me to Hell." *

entries.author: TheBit
entries.body: Prancer smiles. "I know the answer is buried in your name, but why do you assume they immediately want us dead?"

entries.author: BGM
entries.body: “Then we’ll have 300 yards of a choke point for you cover us! It would be single file for them as well if they’re dumb enough to follow.  Should be easy enough for you, right?!”

entries.author: The_Frostrune
entries.body: "Yeah.  Sure."  The dead look that accompanies the words leave little doubt to their true meaning.

entries.author: Kartoonstew
entries.body:
"fuckin ell, you guys smell that? smells like a raccoon got buried up me asshole and went to see the allfather." Tulip pauses. The realization slowly sets in. "oh, fuckin ell, it's me innit? its' fuckin me. right, you lot decide, but fixin to find me a wash tub i am on the other side."

"iffin we find erselves in combat, make sure ye take some mortal wounds. could use some practice i could."

entries.author: The_Frostrune
entries.body: Gallows raises an eyebrow at the odd comments from Tulip, shakes his head in exasperation, and says "If its settled, can we get this death march started then?  At least I'll actually see water again before I die."

entries.author: BGM
entries.body:
“You’re welcome to stay here with your backside up in the air,  if permitted.  I would be more than happy to walk the bridge by myself and try to gain entrance.  If they shoot at me crossing the bridge that they don’t seem to concerned about guarding (as mentioned above), then we’ll know where they stand, and we try plan B or C.”

“I didn’t get this old without scars standing around wondering ‘what if’.  If you have a better idea, like the one you presented earlier, Gallows, that no one seems to be excited about (unless I, Mark, missed something), I am all ears and all for it.  Whatever we decide, I suggest, with all due respect, that we make a decision and do it because I would rather not sit here all afternoon and tomorrow with my ass STUCK TO THIS COLD FUCKING ROCK!”

“Fuck! Sorry.  Apologies, Sarge. I’ll dig latrines at the next camp if you see fit.”

entries.author: The Idle Villager#OG1
entries.body:
“For Christ’s sakes, we’ve spent nine days talking about this and the best we got is…walk into the City lined up like a bunch of lemmins. I ain’t never been tutored or read much or wrote much, but I know it’s good sense to have an exit plan and a good idea or three of how I might wanna get out of a place if the shit goes down.”

Herbie pauses for at least ten seconds, with a confused look as if he forgot what he was going to say.  Then before speaking again, he slides his tongue around and in and out of a what few teeth he has remaining.   

“Listen (*with a slight whistle* as he pronounces his s’s), methinks we should scout the river and area surrounding the city, and find a few exit pats, pass, pathth, goddammit, a few ways to leave that city before we trap ourselfesses in what sounds like a shithole of a city.”  

“Shit, my brothers, iffin these were welcoming people, seems like them woulda paid us a visit by now.  Seein’ how they been riding them camels and shit and knewed we was here setting up camp and shit.  I mean what we doing here.” 

“I ain’t no scout and I ain’t that quiet but I know a thing about surviving and walking in the front door grinning like jackasses eating briars seems like dead men walking to me, but I like to crack skulls with this ball of pointy steel on this thunderstick.  So I’ll do just fine either way…”

Herbie stops talking and starts whistling a little tune or you think that’s what he’s doing but it’s hard to know since he whistles inadvertently when he talks…

“Time is on my *side*…yes it is…”

entries.author: Kartoonstew
entries.body: "Thank ye, claude opus"

entries.author: The Idle Villager#OG1
entries.body: Haha.  This one I wrote, 100% on my own from my phone, while I used Claude Cowork from my work laptop to test replacing outsourced accountants in the near future.

entries.author: BGM
entries.body:
Grimace takes a long deep breath and exhales through his nose, silently counting to ten.   “Let me explain it this way...
We are clearly concerned about the reception we would receive from the inhabitants within the walls, yes?”
“Are you a sneaky sort, Herbie?  Am I?  No.  Now hold that thought for a moment.”
“Suppose I am in my home.  I see you sneaking around my house. Do you know what I’m going to do?  Probably harm you.  How’s that look?  Suspicious, right?  Now suppose you casually walk up to my door and knock, or I see you casually walking up to my door.  What am I going to do?  I’m going to halt you and ask you a series of questions to determine if you’re a threat.  If you are, I’ll harm you.  If I determine you are not, I will talk with you.”
“Le’s talk disguise.  If you make it in my house and I find out you’re not who you present yourself to be; if I don’t harm you, I certainly won’t trust you.”
Grimace looks around to all of you, “You see where I’m going with this?”

entries.author: BGM
entries.body:
“Now, back to the sneaky part.  Are we all going together to sneak around?  Probably not because as I pointed out, your job (points to Herb) is to smash things (unless Mark is mistaken but let’s just assume not for right now), mine is to tell you to GET THE FUCK OUT OF THE WAY of incoming attacks and to step to your right so you can get a better angle of attack.  And you know what?  You and I are damn good at what we do.  Do you know what we’re not good at? SNEAKING AROUND!  Gallow’s is the sneaky sort.  So, let’s assume Gallows is sneaking around trying to find another way in and gets caught.  He’s FUCKED! Unless we’re all there, we or he might have a chance, but we would certainly be caught since we may as well be walking around with a FUCKIN marching drummer boy.  Our gig is up; we’re not getting anything out of here from that point.”
“Let’s touch lightly on the disguise option.  Maybe we will get in.  Disguise gets discovered.  Trust is lost.  End of story.  Oh, one last thing?  Do you know what I’m not good at?  Disguises.”

entries.author: BGM
entries.body:
“None of the suggestions are a terrible idea.  The only idea that’s not going to work is sitting here talking about what may or may not work and doing nothing.  Do you know what idea is likely to answer the question of whether we would be ‘welcomed’ with less chance of collateral damage?  Me, walking across the bridge, maybe with one other of you who may have balls, and ‘asking’ if we can trade, water our horses, sing campfire songs, or WHATEVER!  Admittedly, after reconsideration, one or two of us is probably better than all of us, either way.  I would happily volunteer.  If I get shot at, attacked or whatever, then we know what we need to know and you can try something else.  If I don’t, then I can make a path to bring the rest of you in.”
“Oh, but dear Grimace, what if you get killed? (he shouts to himself)”
“I’m old boys.  I’m old because I ain’t that easy to kill.”
OOC: I promise to tone down the profanity and assholishness in person.  I love you all.

entries.author: BGM
entries.body: OOC: also sorry for the shitty format.

entries.author: Fitz
entries.body: Bumble looks at Grimace, a brief wave of adoration washing across his face.  "This is wisdom...but I wonder if we should ALL go and let you do the talking, eh?  I sense that we may not get another chance to work together for another 8  months at least, so staying together might make things less boring for the brothers picking they taints back here."

entries.author: Catfish
entries.body: Twitch shrugs, almost imperceptibly. "Ain't no bloke gonna look twoice a' me if'n I chum up w me slumfolk, and I could gets us at least some infamation 'at moit be 'elpful. 'En again it moit not be  'elpful. Up to you lofty pigfuckas, all the saim ta me."

entries.author: The_Frostrune
entries.body:
Immediately after the fight with our ancient black brothers..,

“Erlik’s black balls - that was a desperate scrap!   The Dick is dead.  Tadpole lost a hand. And the rest of us lost enough blood to float a barge!!   Death mocks me I tell you.  Some great cosmic joke to watch me dance ‘ere sweet release.

entries.author: The_Frostrune
entries.body: “Am I crazy or did those undead brothers salute us before they fell; like a thank you for releasing them from some long tortured vow?”

blocks.text: I am the Annalist. It is my job to record what happens. The problem, as anyone who has held this post more than a season will tell you, is that "what happens" and "what Brothers say happened" are two different rivers that only rarely run the same course.

runs.text: I am the Annalist. It is my job to record what happens. The problem, as anyone who has held this post more than a season will tell you, is that "what happens" and "what Brothers say happened" are two different rivers that only rarely run the same course.

blocks.text: What follows is my best reconstruction of the Knuckle's time in Caras. I was not there. I got it from them, which means I got pieces of it, in the wrong order, with contradictions smoothed over and inconveniences quietly buried. Gallows tells stories the way a man plays cards — he shows you enough to hold your interest but never the whole hand. Grimace tells stories the way a man falls off a statue — loudly, all at once, with no useful detail. Twitch barely tells stories at all. I believe I have the shape of it right. Some of the dates are guesses. One or two scenes I have reconstructed from what seemed likely given the participants. Any man who objects to my reconstruction is welcome to write his own version. None of them will.

blocks.text: Caras is not a city so much as a market that got ambitious. Permanent walls of mudbrick, yes, but half of them crumbling, and the other half propped up by tents and canvas that lean against the stone like tired men against a fence. In the days before the Trade Festival, the whole place smells of roasted meat, animal dung, fatesh, and the particular human smell that accumulates when several thousand people gather in a desert with no love of bathing. This I have seen with my own eyes, and needed none to tell me.

Herbie, in the way of a man who has spent too long thinking about the interior of the human body, reportedly examined the women's teeth before engaging them in any other capacity. They are the Brotherhood of Ash, the Ikhwan al-Ramad, who preach that the world ended long ago and everything since has been an elaborate afterthought. They smell of smoke and incense and something older underneath, like hot stone. Some of the Knuckle took the blessing. Others did not. Gallows took it, which surprises me; he is not a devout man. blocks.text: There is a specific quality to heat in a port city that is unlike any other heat I have experienced in my twenty-seven years of campaign. It sits in the air like wet wool. It gets into the stones at noon and breathes back out at midnight, so there is no hour at which the body can fully surrender to rest. The Red Lake to the north feeds the whole coast with its particular humidity and the men hated it with a focused intensity that kept them occupied in lieu of anything useful to do.

blocks.text: We did not, however, do it during the month of Qassad. We didn't do anything in Qassad except walk streets and break up gatherings and stand between people who wanted very badly to hit each other, which is the least dignified use of a military outfit this side of decorative flagpole standing. The Emir had a problem: a significant portion of Gjol Port's population believed his city's future lay in a formal alliance with Muirthemne before the war with Rhi'Anon that everyone seemed to know was coming and no one seemed able to stop. These people were not wrong, exactly — there was an argument to be made for their position — but they were inconvenient, and their inconvenience expressed itself in public gatherings that occasionally became something more kinetic, and the Emir's own garrison was not a reliable tool for managing people whose cousins were in that garrison.

blocks.text: Word arrived that a man named Tariq was drinking at the Nets and would likely be gone within a day or two. Tariq was the former harbormaster of Gjol Port — which meant he knew the approaches, the tides, the shoals and channels of the Gjol River and the Red Lake both, better than any man alive. If he reached Thar Anos and put that knowledge in the Prince's hands, the operation we were building toward became considerably more difficult.

It is a two-story timber building on a narrow lane near the lower district — three old fishing nets nailed across the upper facade by way of signage, a thick scarred door, wooden shutters hanging unevenly from rusted hinges. blocks.text: Every veteran in the flotilla understood the arrangement before anyone said it aloud. You put the mercenary companies on the boats and you march the army overland in the heat, and when you arrive at the walls, the mercenaries go first. This is not cruelty; it is arithmetic. It is an ancient calculation and it is not wrong. It is simply the contract stripped to its skeleton.

blocks.text: Thar Anos sits atop a basalt spur above a bend in the river. The walls are tiered. The towers are real. Someone built this fortress to actually hold against a serious assault, which is rarer than you'd think; most fortifications you encounter in this profession were built to impress and defend against the merely desperate. Thar Anos was built by Muirthemne at its height, which means it was built by people with the engineering talent and the political will to do the thing properly.

He took Thar Anos twenty years ago in a border war and kept it by being the kind of man who could keep it. Not a mad tyrant, not a petty lord playing at rebellion. blocks.text: There is a specific joy in sacking, which I record without apology because denying it would be dishonest. After weeks of peacekeeping misery and then a sustained brutal assault that cost blood at every stage, a taken fortress represents several things simultaneously: survival, completion, and the tangible proof that the effort was worth something. blocks.text: I will not dwell on the march. I will record it briefly and accurately: two weeks west from Thar Anos along the Gjol Walk in the worst heat of the campaign season, which means the worst heat most of them had experienced in their professional lives. The Walk is not a road. It is a direction — west, always west — and it offers the marching man approximately nothing in the way of comfort. Little water. Less shade. The sun by midday turned the ground into something that seemed to push heat upward from beneath as well as pound it down from above, so you were being cooked from both directions simultaneously.

blocks.text: CARAS — Day of Salt through Dathra, Year of Dust 47

runs.text: CARAS — Day of Salt through Dathra, Year of Dust 47

blocks.text: The Knuckle arrived at Caras on the Day of Salt. Seven men, intact, no incidents on the road worth recording. They found the city, assessed it, and were assessed by it in the manner of men who have been in enough places to know when a place is deciding what it thinks of them.

blocks.text: They were summoned by Wali Marid within the week. Handled it correctly — Company business goes through you, not them, they are not authorized to negotiate, good day. Marid accepted this and told them to fetch you. Standard.

runs.text: They were summoned by Wali Marid within the week. Handled it correctly — Company business goes through you, not them, they are not authorized to negotiate, good day. Marid accepted this and told them to fetch you. Standard.

blocks.text: While in the city: one crocodile killed in the Maul, one washerwoman not saved, one dockside altercation with the River Men’s Nalo that ended with a bolt in his shoulder and him in the river. The Copper Men watched all of this. The crocodile business generated goodwill in the slums. I have recorded both in the full Annals.

blocks.text: Marid privately contracted the Knuckle — with your authorization — to extract the Boy Prophet, a child called Keshin, from the Dust Priests before the Festival. His stated reason was the boy’s welfare. His actual reason was political leverage over the Ikhwan al-Ramad. We concluded this afterward. At the time, the mission proceeded.

blocks.text: The Bone Yard extraction went as planned, with one complication worth noting: the boy demonstrated, on the Knuckle, a capability that I will record here plainly and let you make of it what you will. He spoke a word and stopped all seven of them. Completely. Then spoke a second word and released them. He is approximately ten years old. He then walked cooperatively to the safe house, which turned out to be Nalo’s, which told us something about the arrangement we’d been placed inside.

blocks.text: Marid then executed the double-cross you are aware of. He returned the boy to the Priests publicly, named the Black Company as the kidnappers, and purchased himself a festival’s worth of religious goodwill at our expense. Drains brought us this intelligence on the road to Dengbi, sixty miles on foot with a wound in his ribs. The other three — Doubts, Goat, Slick — did not make it out of Caras. I have recorded their names. The ledger on them is not closed but I am not optimistic.

blocks.text: The Nets Tavern: the Knuckle was sent to acquire Tariq, the former harbormaster, before he could reach Thar Anos. The intelligence was false. The Nets had been prepared as an ambush — forty-plus rebels, staged, with Mercy’s reserve deliberately delayed. Samir, the Emir’s second son, had provided and shaped the false intelligence. Seven men killed twenty-nine rebels in that building and all seven walked out. I wrote the number down three times because the first two times it looked wrong.

blocks.text: The Knuckle entered this period as seven men and closed it as six. They have, in the span of roughly one campaign season, abducted a child prophet who can stop men dead with a word, survived a forty-man ambush in a tavern, found a Brother hung on a wall and settled that debt quietly, taken a fortress by climbing what used to be scrubbrush, and inherited the charge of nine ancient Brothers who gave up death to stand watch over something that should not be let out.

entries.author: TheBit
entries.body:
Prancer walks around and casually rolls over the bodies on the floor retrieving his daggers and darts. Once he is satisfied he has found them all, he stacks one body on top of another, takes off his overcoat and sits on the back of the piled pair of bodies and looks over his overcoat. With a small frown he says almost inaudibly "Damn."

He roots through his pack and finds his sewing kit and pulls out a needle and thread. As he licks the thread and prepares to thread the needle, he notices his Brothers staring at him, some quizzically, some confusedly, and some disgustedly. He shrugs at them, looks down at his tattered overcoat and says “What is put asunder must be made whole again. You cannot make it new, but you can at least make it whole again. Make it serviceable. Make it work.”

“Our little knuckle here has been put asunder a few times since we crossed those steppes, and each time we mend it and make it whole again. But it is never the same. It carries scars, just like this coat. We have lost Herbie and The Dick, and it is only through skill and fortune we have not suffered more loss. Death is part and parcel with what we do as Brothers, but it hurts no less.”

“I feel like The Black has been put asunder and must be made whole again. I think that is why The Captain had us cross the steppes. I don’t get very sentimental when it comes to the reading of the annals, but I do think The Black Company was greater in its past, more purposeful, dare I say noble at times. I think maybe The Captain wants that for The Black again. Of course, maybe I am wrong and completely full of shit.”

entries.author: TheBit
entries.body:
Prancer puts a hand on the shoulder of the dead Brother he is seated on. “I think these Brothers had purpose and that purpose was not simply hiring on to fight wars, plunder stores and bed whores. In spite of my baser instincts, I think that appeals to me.”

“We don’t know anything about this land. I just hope The Black manages to be on the right side of whatever conflicts we get involved in. It is unclear what was going on here with these Brothers or why they were protecting it, but I think we need to find out. I hope Croaker can pull something from the Annals to help clue us in. I’m going to pack up those Annals in the corner and get them to him. The Black Company was on this side of the steppes. Who would have guessed?”

Prancer winces as he sticks his thumb with the needle, stares at the small drop forming, and laughs softly. “More blood. I thought for sure I had seen the last of it for this day.” He sucks the blood off his thumb, looks at it briefly, then goes back to work mending his coat.

entries.author: The_Frostrune
entries.body: When the adrenaline starts to wear off, Gallows puts his back against an empty space of wall and slides to the floor with a audible groan.  "Fuck me.  My scars are gonna have scars before we leave this fuckin' desert."

entries.author: The_Frostrune
entries.body: He stares at the ancient banner, the book, and the undead bodies of their ancient Brothers on the floor.  "What are we doing boys?  What is this all here for?  How fuckin' old *IS* the Black?  And what, *the absolute fuck*, is behind that wall <pointing at the seal>?

entries.author: The_Frostrune
entries.body: "Yo Tadpole!  I'll give you a 1/2 bottle of Mezcal to stop whinging about your hand and give us some answers; maybe read that book?"

entries.author: Fitz
entries.body: The fact a previous wizard...and now tadpole...have made contact with something so awful, something beyond that seal...that they both had their hand chopped off...well whatever it is, I don't think we're ready for it. I say we get the fuck out of here.

entries.author: smalls
entries.body: Tadpole nods, still grimacing in pain, still waiting for Tulip to do his damned job and bind his severed arm. "Whatever is behind that seal, it's...it's more a *presence* than a creature. Strong. Incredibly strong. Probably like a CR for seven 15th level characters with good players behind each of them."  He drags himself to his feet. "I'd take the book. Like Prancer, I think there's a reason we're here - not just the hopes of loot, of which I see none. The Old Man will want to know the Black was here the gods only know how long ago." He begins to wrap an old cloak about his spurting stump, staring accusingly at Tulip.  "Anyway, I'm with the Bumble. Let's GTFO.  And, no, we're not paying those bandits down below their extra 50 gp."

entries.author: TheBit
entries.body:
Prancer finishes with mending his overcoat and tucks his sewing kit in a pocket within his pack. “I would like to get out of here as quickly as any of you, but I think we need to take some time to rest up. There is not a more secure place to do it than here. I think if we give a wide berth to that seal or whatever it is, we should be fine. Nothing is wandering up here.  I would hate to leave and head back down to those men below in the state we are in only to find out they are shrewd opportunists that love nothing more than taking advantage of weakened marks. I mean, that is what I would do if I were them. Plus, it will give me some time to cozy up with these Annals. I would love to take a closer look.”

Tadpole shrugs and says “He’s not wrong, I suppose. We might as well patch ourselves up and get some rest before we head back down”. He looks around him, spins around in a circle scanning the room. Finally, he looks up and implores “Has anyone seen my hand? I think I’d like to hang on to it.”

entries.author: TheBit
entries.body:
Grimace deadpans “I think it’s sticking out from under that dead Brother over by the seal, unless he sprouted a third hand during the fight. You can get it your damned self.” 

“Meh, it belongs to him now. I’m not getting anywhere near that seal again until I know more about it. I can’t afford to lose this one.” Tadpole quips as he holds up his intact hand.

With that, Prancer spreads out his bedroll and lays on it, rests his head on his pack, cracks open the Annals and begins to thumb through the pages as everyone else goes about settling down to get some rest.

About an hour later, just as everyone is finishing a lackluster meal of dried meat and molded cheese. Prancer sits up and rests the Annals on his lap with an audible sigh and pinches the bridge of his nose. “This is the damnedest, most frustrating thing I have ever seen. The passage that the Annals were open to when we arrived, the one I read to you all right after the fight,  is still perfectly clear to me. When I look at the page without the intention of reading the words, it is in a language I have never seen before. When I concentrate on that page the words just become clear in my mind. I shouldn’t be able to read it, yet I can.”

entries.author: TheBit
entries.body:
Twitch sidles up next to Prancer and peers over his shoulder. “Aye, I can read it too, and I don’t recognize none o’ the letters. Don’t know what’s frustratin’ ‘bout that though Bruv.”

“That is not the frustrating part.” Prancer turns the page. “Read this.”

Twitch scans the page, and his brow furrows. “What the ever-loving fuck Bruv?” He turns his gaze to Prancer who is nodding knowingly.

“Right?” Prancer looks at Twitch. “The same script by all counts, yet I cannot read any other page in this book. It is like the words are right there in my mind yet I cannot find them. I would swear the text moves, no, more like shimmers on the page. Staring at it makes me feel practically nauseated. I would swear this book is trying to keep its secrets.”

Tadpole scurries across the room. “Let me see that.” Tadpole flips the pages back and forth, growing ever more excited with each turn of the page. “Fascinating!”

“So, you can read it then?” Prancer inquires.

“Not a word, Prancer, not a word. Except, of course, for the passage it was open to. I’ve never seen anything like it. Again, utterly fascinating!” Tadpole replies.

entries.author: TheBit
entries.body:
“Fascinating it may be, but how is it possible?” Prancer asks.

“Magic, of course.” Tadpole smirks. “Keep that book safe, Prancer, the Captain will want to see it.”

Prancer holds it out to Tadpole. “Take it then. It seems too important for me to hold on to.”

“What do I look like, some kind of pack mule?” Tadpole scoffs. “No, you hold on to it for now. Who knows , maybe with your penchant for languages, it will reveal its secrets to you. I doubt it, but you never know.”

“You just don’t want to carry it, right?” 

“Right” Tadpole offers a wan smile and holds up his stump. “Besides, how could I?”

Prancer rolls his eyes, wraps up the book, and stuffs it into his pack.

entries.author: The_Frostrune
entries.body: "Hey Tadpole, what do we do about them magic wards you dropped so we could get to this chamber?  Like.. can you put them back?  Can any knucklehead now walk in here and touch the wall and crack it like a thin sheet of ice?"

entries.author: smalls
entries.body:
Tadpole, for a moment, looks at Gallows as if he had sprouted four horns and had winged unicorns fly out his nostrils. "P-put...put them back?" 

The wizard lays a hand - his only hand - against his chest. "Why, Brother Gallows, I am a capable wizard, no doubt. But...tell me: could you build a warship? An honest to goodness warship. Sleek hull, two masts and a mizzen, excellent rigging? No? Right - of course you couldn't. None of us could.  But," the chubby wizard holds up a finger and smiles, "you could burn one to the waterline. You and the other lads here."

Gallows frowns. "Your point?"

"My point, sir," Tadpole says as if imparting a great lesson, "is that it is much, much easier to *break* things - to destroy them, to burn them - than it is to *build* things." He sighs. "So, no, I can't put the wards back. But it doesn't matter - because the wards are still there. Cracked a bit, maybe, but...still there. Stronger than anything I've ever seen.  And unless someone knows how to travel to the astral - and I know of no one save a particular hermit who's about thirty years in the grave and two thousand miles east of us - that can do that...except me. This room, sir, is safe."

entries.author: The_Frostrune
entries.body: Gallows squints , looks Tadpole dead in the eye for a couple long seconds, then shrugs,  “Works for me.”  "Let's get the fuck outta here."

entries.author: smalls
entries.body:
Tadpole lets anyone other than him take point and lead the knuckle out of Telembor. The brigands on the ground floor apparently didn't wait for their 50 gp. "Like as not," Twitch says, glancing around their abandoned camp and still smoldering fire pit, "they fled when they heard the sand wraiths or us screaming up above."

Grimace grunts. "Smart ."

Tadpole winces in pain and looks out onto the desert and the Gjol Walk road. "I figure we wait for the Company - they have to pass here on their way from Thar Anos. Or, we head to Muirthemne and ready the welcome wagons for them." He shoots an accusatory glance at Tulip before adding, "Unless I bleed out first ."

entries.author: The_Frostrune
entries.body: “We’re not getting to either tonight.  I say we set up camp in that cave with the fresh water spring.  Rest.  Eat. Figure out our next move?”   Gallows looks for any objections, seeing none - he starts heading off toward the correct entrance.

entries.author: smalls
entries.body:
**Wherein the Devil’s Knuckle Gets Some Pussy**

Tadpole, in the manner of most wizards – or, at least, in the manner of the three wizards you guys know – is the last to wake. He does so with noises. A loud sigh when Gallows nudges him with a boot toe. A grunt when Twitch pokes him with the limb of his crossbow. A groggy snarl - “I’m up, man, I’m up!” - when Bumble kicks the wizard in the side.

Tulip squats down, eye-level with the wizard. “Show me the arm.” 

Grimace strides to where Twitch is looking, a hand shielding his gaze from the beating sun. “He’s alone,” Twitch says. Then, at Grimace’s raised brow, “He’s one of ours.”

A lone figure makes his way toward the Drum of Telembor, the rising sun at his back. It takes some time – a man can see a long, long way on those brown plains. Prancer’s the first to call it: “Pussy.”

Pussy arrives just as the knuckle is packed and ready to move. The grizzled man bends over, places his hands on his knees. He’s as drenched as if he had just climbed from the Maul. “You can’t be serious.”

“We are,” Grimace says. “Need to move.”

At Pussy’s look, Twitch shrugs apologetically. “There were raiders here. They left. Don’t know if they’re coming back. Don’t know if they’ve got friends.”

Pussy straightens. Accepts a flask of water from Bumble. Drinks like his life depends on it. “Where to, then?”

Tulip wraps up some still somewhat-white bandages and thrusts them in his satchel. He stands. “Muirthemne. That’s where the Company’s heading, ‘lest something changed?”

entries.author: smalls
entries.body:
Pussy shakes his head. “I won a couple big pots in Tonk. A couple pots that Mercy thought were his to win.” He takes another pull from the flask, hands it back. “Fucker sent me on ahead to find you boys. No camel nor nothing neither.”

“Orders?” Grimace asks, all business.

Pussy wipes sweat from his brow. “Get to Muirthemne. Secure a barracks. See which way the wind blows.”

Grimace nods. “Fair enough. We know some names.”

Tadpole clambers to his feet. “Bugger me!” Pussy breathes, wide-eyed. “What in the black balls happened to your damned hand?”

“Tulip,” answers Tadpole. “Tulip happened.”

entries.author: smalls
entries.body:
**Wherein the Knuckle Arrives at Muirthemne**

The smell reaches you before the walls do. Orange blossom and charcoal smoke and the particular sweetness of overripe dates fermenting in the heat. Then the walls themselves — sandstone the color of old bone, stained darker at the base where the centuries have accumulated — and above them the minarets catching the last copper light of the afternoon. From somewhere inside a call to prayer beginning its long, patient climb into the sky. 

You have been told that Muirthemne is a city in decline. Standing at its gates with the dust of the Gjol Walk still on your boots, eight days from the Drum, you understand that Muirthemne's decline is considerably more impressive than most cities' heights.

“Big,” Grimace observes. He speaks for all of you.

entries.author: smalls
entries.body:
**OOC**

You scored a Triumph on the Off-Stage Homebrew Adjudication (OSHA) roll last session when Longneck and his Fist were sent to Muirthemene, before they returned to Thar Anos. This was the Annals entry: 

*The Godking's city. I won't pretend I wasn't impressed -- I was, and I'm a man who has seen things that would make the Godking's architects weep with inadequacy. But the city is not the point. The point is we left with contacts and potential patrons and the kind of relationships that take years to build and that other outfits would kill for. Literally kill for. The Captain is going to need a bigger ledger.*

You stand outside the open gates to Muirthemene, capitol of the Empire of the same name. Impossibly old. Impossibly large. Twenty Gjol Ports could fit within the circumference of its walls. You’ve been tasked with finding a barracks in anticipation of the Company’s arrival. You know names. Three to be exact:

•    **Nazim al-Yusri**, a mid-level yet influential functionary in the Godking’s court
•    **Bassam ibn Tariq**, a fabulously wealthy, and fabulously arrogant, olive oil merchant
•    **Qasim al-Dhahabi**, an unscrupulous and feared moneylender  

You have some time before the Company arrives. Probably two weeks, at the shortest.  They speak Muir here, with a decent smattering of Rhish and Maulik.

Make me proud.

entries.author: TheBit
entries.body: Prancer looks over the sweat-drenched, travel-weary lot that is his companions and says "Men, the hard work is done here. The Black is already seen positively by some folks. I have the utmost confidence we can fuck that up in the short amount of time before the rest of our ranks arrive."

entries.author: Fitz
entries.body:
Bumble spits dust, wipes his mouth with the back of his hand, and studies the gates a long moment. “Big,” he says, echoing Grimace, but quieter. Like he’s already thinking past it.

He shifts his shield, checks the straps out of habit. “Big means we disappear easy. Also means we can get lost just as easy.”

A glance back at the crew. At Tadpole’s ruined hand. 

“We don’t know the streets. Don’t know the players. Only names.” He taps two fingers against his temple. “Names are a start.” He jerks his chin toward the open gate.

“Step one—we get inside before dark. Find a tavern that don’t ask questions and ain’t too clean. Somewhere the kind of people we’re looking for might hear about us before we go knocking.”

A beat.

“Step two—we pick one of those names and make the first move. Not all three at once. That’s how you look desperate.”

He rolls his shoulder, settling into the weight of his gear.

“Moneylender hears everything. Merchant knows everyone. Court man moves slow but pulls strings.” A faint shrug. “Depends what kind of trouble we want first.”

Then, flat: “I say we get a drink, listen a while, and then go introduce ourselves proper to one of them. Quiet-like.”

He starts toward the gate without waiting for agreement. “Standing out here makes us look like we don’t belong.”

entries.author: The_Frostrune
entries.body:
"Hey!  Remind me again, is this city allied with the Emir of Gjol Port or with the rebels we just spanked?"

“Gjol Port, you dipshit,” Grimace says with a shake of his head.  

Ignoring the insult Gallows responds, “Good.  The news of battle at Thar Anos should have reached here by now.  The Black should have some Rep rolling in.  We’ll be on the good side of the authorities… at least for bit.”

A few more steps down the road and Gallows chimes in again, “Hey Pussy – you sure the orders were to find a barracks?  Isn’t that usually provided by our Patron?”  He looks around at the rest of group looking for nods or correction.  Everyone is too hot and miserable to care to make eye contact.

“Fucked if I know,” Pussy spits back, “That’s what Mercy said, *Find a barracks*.”

“Well…”, Gallows continues, “Does that mean we are doing the talking for the Company and securing a Patron?  I mean, we aren’t equipped for that.”

“Shut it Gallows!” Grimace barks.  “There’s enough hot air already without you blatherin’ on.”

Prancer pulls a semi clean handkerchief from his sleeve and dabs his brow.  “He’s not wrong.  Usually the place we are garrisoned is supplied by the Patron or we negotiate the costs into the terms.  I doubt Mercy meant for us to start negotiations…”

Pussy interrupts, “He fuckin’ said*** Find. A. Barracks.***  Do what you want but don’t get pissed at me when he flies off the handle!”

“Look,” Prancer continues a little exasperated, “Let’s take Bumble’s advice and find a mid-tier inn.  Get some good food and drink, maybe a bath; and discuss our next steps when we are in better spirits.  Agreed?"

entries.author: smalls
entries.body: The city swallows you whole before you've cleared the gate shadow. Muirthemne does not ease you in — it simply begins. A palanquin shoulders past without ceremony, its silk curtains the color of a bruise, four slaves moving beneath it with the practiced indifference of men who have long since stopped seeing the faces watching them. From a minaret three stories above the nearest lane a mufti leans into open air, one hand gripping stone, the other raised to heaven, his call to prayer unspooling above the noise of the street like smoke above a fire. Nobody looks up. They have heard it every day of their lives. You have not. Somewhere further in, past a tangle of awnings and argument, a man in a scorched robe spins a khopesh wreathed in pale flame, his eyes on the blade rather than his audience.

entries.author: smalls
entries.body: The streets narrow and widen without logic, opening into small squares choked with pigeons and commerce, then contracting again to passages barely wide enough for two men abreast. The smell changes with each turn — cardamom, rendered fat, cut stone, something sharp and chemical from a dyer's workshop, then the faint green smell of water from somewhere below street level. You pass a wall covered floor to ceiling in blue tile, every tile a different shade, the whole thing cohering into a pattern only visible from a distance none of you can achieve on this street. You pass a boy sitting cross-legged on a step, reading aloud to himself from a scroll he holds upside down. You pass a door that is simply open, and inside it a very old man sitting at a very large table covered in birds — live birds, perched on his arms and shoulders and the back of his chair — and he is speaking to them in a low continuous murmur, and none of them fly away.

entries.author: smalls
entries.body: The inn is called the Four Towers, though only three of them are still standing, and only two of those are connected. The ground floor is a common room in the conventional sense — low ceiling, long tables, a kitchen visible through a smoke-stained arch — but the rooms are not below. They are above. Each tower has been subdivided into open-air platforms, roofed with canvas that rolls back in fair weather, walled with screens of carved wood that let the night air through. The platforms are connected where they can be — two of the three towers share a rope bridge wide enough for one man at a time, which sways with the confidence of something that has not yet killed anyone and intends to keep the streak alive. Your table is on the highest platform of the middle tower, twenty feet above the street, far enough from the nearest occupied platform that conversation stays where you put it. A boy operates a rope-and-pulley system from below — you lower a basket, you raise it full. The bread is fresh. The beer is cold in the way that only old stone and deep cisterns can manage in this heat. The city spreads in every direction, flat and enormous and lit amber by the last of the day, minarets catching the light above the roofline like fingers.

entries.author: smalls
entries.body:
Tadpole produces a scrap of leather from somewhere inside his robe — not paper, leather, stiff and dark — and a stick of charcoal, and he sets about writing with the focused deliberateness of a man relearning a thing he thought he knew. His left hand. He gets there. The letters are large and uneven and unmistakably his.

**Nazim al-Yusri **— Court. Katib al-Sirr.
**Bassam ibn Tariq **— Merchant. Olive oil.
**Qasim al-Dhahabi **— Moneylender.

He sets the leather on the table and turns it so you all can read it.
"Way I see it," he says, not looking up yet, still studying what he wrote, "each of these men wants something. Maybe we need to figure which one wants it bad enough?" He looks up. "Not for us to contract with someone - that's the Captain's purview. But we should have a recommendation when they arrive, I think."

entries.author: Fitz
entries.body:
Bumble leans back just enough to look out over the city, then forward again to the scrap of leather. He taps the last name with a thick finger. “Qasim.” No flourish. Just the word. “Moneylender’s got his fingers in everything. Debts, favors, grudges. People talk when they owe. More when they can’t pay.” A pause. “If there’s wind to read in this place, he’ll know which way it’s blowing.”

He glances at Tadpole’s writing, then at Grimace. “Court man’s slow. Too many doors between us and him. Merchant’ll want coin or contracts we ain’t got authority to offer.” A small shrug. “Qasim? He’ll talk if he thinks there’s profit in it. Or trouble. We can be either.”

He takes a pull of his drink, sets it down. “We don’t promise nothing. We don’t negotiate terms. We listen. Ask the right questions. Figure who’s worth the Captain’s time.” A pause. “Then we find this Qasim before someone else finds us first.”

entries.author: The_Frostrune
entries.body: "I'm fine with talking to the shady guy first.  More our style anyway.  Are we **all** supposed to drag along to these discussions?  Prancer is our only guy that can speak this particular flavor of 'sandy'; he's gotta go.  Should at least send a few others to discourage anyone from gettin' froggy."

entries.author: The_Frostrune
entries.body: "Maybe a second group looks for a foreign quarter or an area where foreign merchants congregate?  We could probably find some others that speak Malik and maybe just get some general wind?"

entries.author: Fitz
entries.body:
Bumble grunts once, more agreement than enthusiasm. “Split’s fine. City’s too big to walk it twice.”  He looks around the table, measuring.  “But not thin.  I'm thinking Prancer's group goes to talk to the shady guy.  I'm in that group, because that group's roleplaying.  But, Prancer needs a spine behind him, not a parade. Three, maybe four total [but if dudes are into this, we can retcon that suggestion.]” 

His gaze shifts to the rest. “Other group keeps it simple. Find the foreign quarter, ears open, mouths mostly shut. We’re not here long enough to get clever.”

He pauses.  “If anything smells off, we don’t chase it. We regroup back here.”

He glances back at the leather, at Qasim’s name. “Last thing we do is get separated in a city like this and start making decisions without each other.”

He reaches for his drink again.  “Let's pick groups.”

entries.author: Fitz
entries.body: [Proposal: if you respond by this time tomorrow, I propose you go in the group attempting to meet with Qasim, the Moneylender.  If you don't, you suck, and you're part of the Annals written about the barracks search or foreign quarter thing.  Thoughts?  If good, feel free to just delete this part of the post if we're keeping it clean...ish.]

entries.author: smalls
entries.body:
[OOC: I'll continue this for the guys who are interested. I can do a separate foreign quarter one if anyone wants to go that route.]

**Qasim al-Dhahabi, Moneylender**
The gate to his compound is iron and guarded by men who look at you the way men look at things they have already decided about. Outside the gate, bound to a post, are two men. They are alive. They are not conscious. Nobody mentions them.
Qasim meets you at the gate himself and walks you inside at a pace that is not hurried. The compound is large and walled and self-sufficient in the way of a place that has considered the possibility of siege. At its center an artesian well bubbles into a stone basin. He stops there, in the shade, and gestures for you to sit.
He is not a large man but he takes up space in the way that has nothing to do with size. His beard is oiled. His eyes are still. A slave attends him without being summoned.

entries.author: smalls
entries.body:
He says, "I am Qasim ibn Musa al-Dhahabi. You are my guests. This is my home. I have nineteen sons. I have two hundred and six head of Meshian camel, with two more expected any day. I have twenty-four wives, of whom only three enjoy my seed.”

He leans back. The slave oils his beard. He lets the silence sit for a moment before continuing. "I tell you these things not to boast, my guests. I tell you them to show you that I am in earnest. And earnest men do not waste the time of other earnest men.”

He looks at each of you in turn. He does not hurry this. "So. You are the Company. Tell me about yourselves."

entries.author: Fitz
entries.body:
Bumble doesn’t rush to fill the silence. Lets it sit. Lets Qasim look. Then, finally, speaking through an interpreter if necessary: “We’re not much for counting what we’ve got.” Bumble shifts slightly in his seat, armor creaking softly. “We count what we finish.” He nods once toward the gate, toward the men tied there. “Looks like you do the same.” 

He pauses. “The Company’s coming. We’re ahead of it. Told to find a place to stand and get a sense for the ground before boots hit it.” He rests his forearms on his knees, steady. “City this size, there’s always work. Trouble somebody wants handled. Quiet or loud.” His eyes meet Qasim’s, not challenging—just level. “We’re here to learn who’s worth listening to. Who’s got problems that pay to solve...and who’s got the reach to make it matter when they do.” 

He leans back slightly. “You struck me as a man who’d know.”

entries.author: The_Frostrune
entries.body: Gallows leans in and whispers  in Khato, "I think he was asking us to introduce ourselves.  Prancer?  Grimace?  Wanna chime in here?"

entries.author: TheBit
entries.body:
Prancer takes a step forward, bows his head slightly then raises his head to address Qasim. “Firstly, thank you for meeting with us and inviting us into your home. You are most gracious. May I add that despite your attempt at modesty, your estate is most impressive. May I call you Qasim, or is there an honorific you would prefer instead? Forgive me, as I have no desire to offend.” 

“My brothers call me Prancer, but my mother first called me Hamilton.” Prancer pauses for just a moment. “Hamilton Langley”.
A slight smile passes across Prancer’s face “Forgive me, the name sounds foreign even to my ears. It is so rare for me to be called anything other than Prancer.” He shakes his head. “I digress.”

“As far as our Brotherhood? We are, as you put it, ‘earnest men’. I could regale you with unceasing accounts from the pages of our annals that go back centuries, and I will, at a later time, if it is your want. I would not lie to you, some of those accounts would be served with a healthy dollop of artistic embellishment. The annals tell us of who we are, who we were, and who we continually strive to be. Suffice it to say, we are good at what we do. There is no embellishment in saying that. While I would not dare say our current complement rivals the sheer numbers and skill of The Company at its zenith, we are still a most capable unit.”

“As Brother Bumble alluded to, the primary reason we have sought you out today is to find out if there is a place to set down our packs and garrison when the rest of our complement arrives. I would say any place that could accommodate, say, 500 men. We don’t know if such a place exists here, but we expect that you would. We are not accustomed to the creature comforts, so our requirements are quite modest. In return for this service, we would of course offer recompense, whether it be remuneration or a service rendered.”

entries.author: TheBit
entries.body:
“Once that is settled, we would, as Brother Bumble also said, like to get the lay of the land. Our charge is not to seek employment for The Company, but The Captain would certainly appreciate a head start on who is in the market for our services.” Prancer’s expression grows stern, something you rarely see from him. “To be clear, we are mercenaries through and through. We pride ourselves on getting the job done. We are not squeamish. What others will not or cannot do, whether it be out of fear or inadequacy, The Black Company can and will do…for the right price.”

His face lightens again and he adds with a slight laugh, “Of course, if you know of any high paying, easy work, we’d be interested in that too.”

Prancer bows slightly then takes a step back to fall in with his Brothers.

entries.author: smalls
entries.body:
Qasim bows his head in return. "*As-salāmu ʿalaykum*. Qasim is just fine. My father was a camel drover. " He waves the slave away. "The city is large, as you have no doubt seen. Five hundred men, you say? Such could be easily swallowed within its belly. Allow me the honor of locating sufficient quarters for you and your Company."

He stands and clasps his hands behind his back. A slave materializes from the shadows and holds a large palm frond above his head.  "Walk with me, if you would be so kind." Without pausing, he begins to stroll. "The Godking in his wisdom has decided that the upstart Rhish must be taught a lesson. How convenient, then, that an army of said upstarts are even now on their way here. I have good word they are approaching Thesh and soon, no doubt, their sandals will slap the sands of what has been Muirthemene territory for ages upon ages."

He pauses, and you find yourself standing with a clear view of the two unconscious men bound to the posts.  "They say war is good for merchants. And perhaps that is even true." He eyes you with a thin smile. "But war is not good to moneylenders, I fear. Especially such lenders who have significant sums invested in men who may not survive the summer.

"I have a request for you. A simple request. I hesitate even to mention it, as trifling as it is." He produces a scroll, sealed with wax.  "A letter must be delivered to a clockmaker on the Street of Defeated Clocks. His name is Faris. Three plant boxes are outside his door. The letter goes under the middle one. You will not speak to Faris or anyone else on that street. You will return here when it is done.”

He measures you for a moment. “The seal is not to be broken. The letter is not to be read. These are the only conditions. A favor for a favor, yes?"

entries.author: The_Frostrune
entries.body:
Now seeing the 2nd pair of men being severely punished, Gallows is more interested.  

Clearly he wanted us to see this. Why?

OOC:  Gallows tries to discretely study the two men.  Anything noteworthy/distinctive?   Are they still alive?  Were they whipped? Starved?  Exposure?  

Perception +4

entries.author: smalls
entries.body: Sorry, it's the same two that you passed upon entering. He just happened to "randomly" walk back toward them while talking. They are alive and unconscious and looks like, from their tattered backs, whipped quite a bit. No markings. Both easterners.

entries.author: The_Frostrune
entries.body: Gallows turns his attention from the beaten men and back to Qasim as he finishes speaking.  "*A simple enough task, probably too simple"*, he thinks.  He looks at the rest of the contingent and seeing no frowns or dissent, he shrugs and steps toward Qasim hand outstreched.  "A simple kindness returned," he slightly bows his head as he accepts the scroll.

entries.author: TheBit
entries.body:
Prancer bows slightly to Qasim then looks to his Brothers. “Well then, let’s see this done.”

Prancer turns and starts walking away from the moneylender’s home. When he is satisfied that they are far enough away from the estate and no one is following them he speaks. “Now why would a man, who has money and slaves, need us to deliver his message? I’m not one to chase conspiracies, but if I were I would wonder if he knew I possess the tools designed to create forgeries. I don’t see how he could, but it is a little too on the nose. I think this is one of three things: a test, a trap, or a trap in the guise of a test. As much as I’d love to crack open that seal, I think we need to play this straight. I also think we don’t need to walk into a trap. I propose we find this Street of Defeated Clocks. We deliver the unopened parchment using a proxy; I suggest using a poor citizen who lives nearby, but not on the street in question to make the drop. We can pay him say 2 gold up front, and 3 more when he returns.”

Prancer pauses for a moment, then frowns. “No, we must assume he is having us followed or owns eyes on that street. While using a proxy to deliver the message is not explicitly against his terms, it is certainly not in the spirit of them. How about I deliver the message? I, or we, would walk past the residence in question a few times and make the drop on one of those passes and use street traffic to hide the delivery.” (OOC: slight of hand on a crowded street after several passes by the flower pots)

“I have several concealed pockets in my fineries. If stopped with the letter still in our possession, we could presumably feign ignorance.” Prancer shrugs, “Of course, I’m open to other ideas.”

entries.author: The_Frostrune
entries.body: "Aye," Gallows winks at Prancer, "I too believe this is a test, my take was more of attention to detail and discretion.  I noted his instructions very carefully* ... we cannot speak to Faris or anyone else on that street*"

entries.author: The_Frostrune
entries.body: "Now how would strangers new to the City find this one clock-guy's shop on a street we have never visited in a city this massive?"  This is Gallows just winding up, thinking he is clever.  "We **have** to ask for directions or we'll never find the place."

entries.author: The_Frostrune
entries.body: "I am thinking proxies just like you," pointing to Prancer.  "We can ask how to find the street of Defeated Clocks then hire a couple urchins to ask about Faris and find his shop.  Two separate street kids, not at the same time.  We tell them to find the place and ask them to provide directions and describe it to us using the three plant boxes to know if they are telling truth.  Assuming the stories match we got our spot.  Whether we trust a kid to deliver it or do it ourselves, haven't got that teased out yet."

entries.author: TheBit
entries.body: "Sounds like as good a plan as any. I would guess that the street in question has water clocks or sundials in disrepair (OOC: unless mechanical clocks exist in this world at this point in time). Ideally, Id like to find out the location without explicitly asking for 'The Street of Defeated Clocks', but for all we know, everyone in Muirthemene except us knows what The Street of Defeated Clocks is and inquiring about it would be no odder than asking where the closest inn is."

entries.author: Catfish
entries.body:
Twitch doesn’t look up from his lap, absent-mendidly checking the tension of the xbow string with fingers that never quite stay still. He spits a bit of Muirthemne dust onto the floor of the Four Towers and finally speaks, his voice a low rasp.

“Urchins are just tiny leaks in a big bucket, lads. You hire a kid to find a shop, and by sunset, every gossip in the district knows someone's looking for the clock-man. Qasim said no talking. I'd say we need to keep this a lot more quite than those youngin's can be.”

He looks at the scroll, then back at his gear, his eyes darting toward the street below.

“Street of Defeated Clocks... If it’s got a name like that, it’s got a look to match. I say we don't ask for directions—we find it with our eyes. I’ll get to a high spot, a minaret or one of these leaning towers, and get the glass on the neighborhood. We find those three planters from a distance, map the exits, and listen to the wind - with our eyes - for a bit. We see who’s watching Faris before we ever set a boot on his cobbles.”

He taps the heavy limb of his crossbow. “Once I’ve got the layout, one of us slips in during a shift change, drops the ink under the middle pot, and vanishes. No urchins to sell our descriptions for a silver, no loose ends. Just a ghost in the shadows. Simple is safe. And safe keeps us from ending up like those miserable saps tied to the gate.”

He looks at Prancer, a thin, cynical smile touching his lips. “I’ll do the scouting. My legs are spindly, but they’re quiet. Just keep the beer cold for when I get back.”

entries.author: Fitz
entries.body: Bumble listens to it all without interrupting. Then: “We’re making this bigger than it is.” He nods once toward Twitch. “He’s right about one thing—quiet matters. Word gets out, we’re done before we start.” Bumble glances to Prancer. “And he’s right too—this smells like a test.” He shifts his weight, armor settling. “So we treat it like one. We don’t break the seal. We don’t use proxies. We don’t get clever.” His eyes move among his brothers'. “Man like Qasim didn’t ask for help because he needs hands. He’s checking if we follow instructions. We find the street with our eyes. No asking. No kids. No chatter." He jerks his chin toward Twitch. “He scouts it. High ground, like he said. We take a look together if we need to. One man makes the drop. Clean. No stopping. No second pass. If something’s wrong, we walk away. Letter stays sealed. We come back and tell him it couldn’t be done clean.” He pauses.  “Better to fail a test than pass a trap.” He pushes off the wall. “Keep it simple. Do it right. Get paid.”

entries.author: The_Frostrune
entries.body: “No harm in us trying to find the street on our own and Farris’ shop. You saw the size of that city. I’m doubting either of those things will be as easy as you make it sound.  Still… no harm in trying ourselves but we can’t take more than a day or so.  If we can’t quickly find it on our own, we’re going to have to ask questions and or get help.  I’m pretty confident we can obscure our involvement if it comes to proxies.”

entries.author: smalls
entries.body:
The approach decided, Twitch sets off in search of something to climb. Onion-domed towers are plentiful; the difficulty lies in finding one that can actually be entered. At last he chooses an abandoned minaret that looks as though his 140 pounds might be enough to bring the whole thing down. He ascends by spiraling, crumbling steps, vanishing and reappearing as the stair coils upward—now enclosed within the tower’s throat, now exposed to the open air before turning inward again.

At the summit he perches like a gargoyle, boots hanging over the edge. Even his silhouette against the sinking sun is enough to stir vertigo. The light fades, and with it Twitch. He returns to the party.

Bumble eyes him. “What’d you find?”

“Jack shit.” Twitch runs a hand through his damp hair. “Could see half the damned city from up there, but it’s just a maze of streets. Aqueducts everywhere—some at rooftop height, some big sons of bitches. Fountains, statues, whole blocks choked with colorful tents, like Caras. A man walks in on one side, I’m not sure he ever walks out the other.”

“Plan B, then.” Gallows exhales. “We spread out. Not tonight. Tomorrow. Walk the streets, eyes peeled, ears open, dicks covered.”

entries.author: smalls
entries.body:
So, come morning, that’s what you do. You move out in pairs. Some of you purchase keffiyehs to shield yourselves from the punishing sun and too many curious eyes. Twitch was right—it’s a maze. Cobbled boulevards lined with date palms give way, without explanation, to winding alleys of hard-packed earth. You pass beneath gates, sandstone arches, and bridges by the dozen, though most of the canals below lie dry and dust-choked. Then, without ever noticing where you turned, you find yourselves walking atop those same bridges and arches, the city rearranged beneath your feet.

Hour by hour, it becomes clear that Muirthemne grows as much upward as outward. You cross a bazaar of windblown grit and ancient paving stones, certain you stand at ground level, only to discover yourselves looking out from a crenellated wall onto a market sixty feet below. Shortly after midday you, miraculously, you all find yourselves back at the initial rendezvous point. The looks on your companions’ faces mirror your own.

“Nothing,” Bumble says, and he speaks for everyone.

“We’re going to have to ask someone,” Prancer says. “Qasim said we were not to speak to ‘Faris or anyone else on that street.’  He never said we couldn’t ask for directions.”

“I don’t like it,” growls Bumble. “But not sure what else we can do.”

entries.author: smalls
entries.body:
After a brief huddle, you decide to let Prancer give it a shot in a nearby caravanserai. He succeeds, quickly and easily. “Draw any attention?” Twitch asks Prancer upon his return.

Prancer shakes his head. “We got to talking, easy enough. He’s proud of his city. A few silvers into the conversation and I couldn’t shut him up. By the time he talked about clocks, I’m pretty sure he thought it was his idea and not mine.” Prancer shrugs. “Anyway, I got a bead on it. Not far from here. Maybe ten blocks.”

You push through crowds in some of the evening bazaars and make your way in the direction Prancer indicates. As you near the street, Twitch separates from the group, his keffiyeh pulled high, and the rest of you sit down outside a restaurant to eat dates, spit seeds, and sip on lemon water.

Twitch returns. “Saw it. Three potted plants, just like we were told. Lots of traffic. It’d be easy, I think, to do the dead drop of the letter and not be seen.”

OOC: If someone is going to do the dead drop – using Sleight of Hand, as you earlier suggested – let me know who it is and what their modifier is.  Feel free, of course, to change your plan.
