entries.author: smalls
entries.body:
Twitch deposits the letter as directed. No bells ring, no cries arise. No one seems to notice. Within a few heartbeats, he is gone.

The next morning, you find yourselves outside Qasim the Moneylender’s compound. The two men once bound to the post remain, though they have progressed from unconscious to dead. Muir flies—iridescent and swollen—buzz about their open mouths. The smell is not ideal.

A slave with a golden nose ring escorts you to the rear of the compound. A silk awning has been raised near the well where you first met Qasim. You are invited to recline on a veritable mountain of cushions, no two alike in color. More slaves arrive to offer lemon water and honeyed locusts.

After some time, Qasim appears. He bows before seating himself. A slave fans him.

“I have found lodging for your Company that, I hope, you will find suitable. It is a warehouse in the Topi district. A safe area for men not of Muir. Wide avenues. Good bazaars. A few decent wineshops. A very good brothel. Two wells, both working—one within, one without.”

Bumble grunts. “How much?”

“Nothing.” Qasim waves a hand bedecked with jeweled rings. “The owner is, quite literally, deeply in my debt. Do you like the locusts?"

Bumble nods. “They ain’t half bad.”

entries.author: smalls
entries.body:
Qasim smiles. It is not a pleasant look. “At the risk of being burdensome, for which I beg your forgiveness, I would ask a second favor. I will not ask a third.”

“You don’t wish to hear about the letter?” Prancer asks.

Qasim shakes his head. “I do not.”

Twitch scratches his neck, eyes darting. “What’s in it for us?” He ignores a look from Gallows. “We did what you asked. You found us lodging. Square trade.”

Bumble picks up Twitch’s line of questioning. “Right. We’re even, Master Qasim. Though we may look a bit rough, we’re not errand boys.”

“Surely.” Qasim tosses a locust into his mouth. “What would you have of me? If it is within my power, it shall be yours.”

Gallows looks from Twitch to Qasim. “Maybe you tell us about this next favor, yes?”

Qasim snaps his fingers. Two veiled guardsmen, on cue, emerge from the shadows of a nearby building. Between them they escort a man. His head is covered by a silk sack. His hands are bound in front of him. His feet are shackled with a short chain that forces him to shuffle forward. Faint bloodstains mark his slippers.

“You deposited a letter. I ask that you now deposit a man. At night. To a location I will provide, should you agree. You will not, of course, attempt to speak with this man, nor will you remove his hood.”

Qasim climbs heavily to his feet. “I will afford you time to discuss this amongst yourselves, should you wish to do so. Merely wave your hand, and I will return.”

He bows and departs.

entries.author: Fitz
entries.body: Bumble watches the man with the hood until Qasim is well gone. He exhales through his nose. “That wasn’t a delivery. That was a leash check.” He looks at the rest of you, one by one. “First job was simple. Quiet. See if we follow orders. We passed. This one’s different." He jerks his chin toward where the prisoner was taken. “Now he wants to see what we’ll carry for him when it ain’t just paper.” Silence hangs a second. “We don’t know who that is. Don’t know where he’s going. Don’t know who we’re crossing by moving him.” His gaze flicks toward the gate—toward where the dead men rot. “We got a hint how he handles things when they go wrong.” He shifts, armor settling. “We’re not here to take contracts. Not yet.” His voice stays even. “Captain decides that. But we are here to figure out who’s worth dealing with. Question is—does doing this tell us more about Qasim…or put us in his pocket before the Company even arrives? If we take it, we do it clean. Same as before. No questions, no mistakes. But we don’t pretend it’s just another errand.”

entries.author: The_Frostrune
entries.body:
Gallows frowns and eyes the retreating prisoner with undisguised concern.    

“Never liked these jobs where you’re  pickin’ sides and don’t know either team.  I’ll do it if that’s the way the vote goes down but I’d rather not. “

“Also don’t want to insult the man.  Clearly (nodding toward the dead men lashed to the posts) he is not a man we want to cross.”

entries.author: TheBit
entries.body: ”I don't think I want any part of this. We've achieved what we needed to achieve. I think it best we thank him again then take our leave. I can only see this ending up with us depleting any credit Longneck and his Fist built up when they arrived within the walls of this city.”

entries.author: Fitz
entries.body:
Bumble listens, and doesn’t argue right away.  Then he clears his throat softly before beginning.  “We already picked a side.”  He nods  toward the compound. “Moment we walked in that gate. Moment we took his help. First job bought us a place to stand. This one tells us what kind of man we’re standing with.”  His eyes light on Gallows.  “You’re right—we don’t know the sides. That’s exactly why this matters. Man like Qasim doesn’t hand out work for no reason. This ain’t about the hooded bastard. It’s about seeing if we’re useful when things get… less clean."  Bumble glances at Prancer.  “You’re worried about burning credit?”  Bumble shrugs.  “Walking away now burns it faster.”  He nods back toward the dead men at the gate. “He offered us something real. We say no on the first hard ask, we’re just another soft outfit that takes favors and won’t return ‘em.”  He pauses.  "We’re the Black.”  His tone is flat and certain.  “We don’t get to be squeamish when the work turns ugly. That’s the work.” He looks between them. “We’re not signing a contract. Not swearing loyalty. We’re moving one man from one place to another and keeping our mouths shut.”  He pauses again.  “And when the Captain gets here, we’ll know exactly what kind of game Qasim’s playing… because we stepped onto the board. Or we walk away, keep our hands clean… and stay blind."

Bumble shifts.  "Personally, I'm all for seeing."

entries.author: Catfish
entries.body: "That idnt how I see it, Bumb. Sure we're mercs - the Black has taken gold from many dirty hands. But idnt it smart to understand the jobs we're taking? Or who we are working for? If we were starving and desperate, yeah maybe it's an easy call. Bu' I fink we've got enough to lose here to fink it through."

entries.author: Fitz
entries.body:
Bumble gives Twitch a small nod. “Ain’t wrong. That’s why we don’t walk in blind—we set the edges first. He pushes off the wall and glances toward where Qasim disappeared. “Let’s find out what kind of leash this really is.”

Bumble raises a hand for the servants. When Qasim returns, he stands and addresses Qasim.  “You said deposit the man. You didn’t say how many it takes to do it."  His tone is even and neutral - business.  “This something you expect a full detail for… or just the job done?”  He pauses.  Bumble then adds, somewhat lamely, "We'll follow your terms - quiet, no talking, no hood off."  He holds Qasim's gaze.  "But how we move him - that's ours to decide?"

And yeah - I know walking into this job without knowing who's in the hood is stupid as fuck and short-sighted - but Bumble's doing it anyway, if you let him.)

So long as you adhere to the simple constraints I have previously articulated, you are free to satisfy the request in whatever fashion you deem most appropriate."

Gallows eyes widen in shock.  Nothing much ever catches him by surprise but Bumble's impulsive response puts him back on his heels.  By the time he fully registers what's happening Bumble is already starting to discuss details with the money-lender!

“Bumble!  What THE fuck are you doing?!  We ain’t there yet.  Sounds to me like the winds blowin’ in the other direction.  You’re puttin’ a mark on our ledger whether you do this by yourself or we all do it.”

Not trying to throw a bucket of water on this (and it may be too late).  Just wanting to make sure everyone who has an opinion gets to respond.

entries.author: TheBit
entries.body:
Prancer looks down and smiles into his chest as Gallows speaks. Gallows catches it and glowers at Prancer “Something funny, Prancer?”

“Yes and no, forgive me. I was not laughing at you, Brother.” Prancers smirk fades and his expression goes to one of casual indifference. “I was merely finding the situation amusing. That is all.”

Clearly annoyed, Gallows barks “Well then again I ask, what’s so fuckin’ funny?” 

Prancer shrugs, “As I said, the situation. I find it hard to worry much about the task at hand. It seems to me in a city this size and this busy, that delivering one anonymous man, whether rolled up in a carpet and dropped off at a doorstep or drug unceremoniously kicking and screaming through the streets, will hardly raise an eyebrow. The vast majority of folks will bury their gaze in the ground as we pass by. The rare would-be hero loses all bravado once a dagger pommel caves in their nose. Guards can be bought off. The task is trivial.”

Prancer’s gaze deliberately moves to Qasim as he next speaks “No, Gallows, what concerns me more with performing this task is what good Qasim here thinks it says about us. Does it say we are mere errand boys? Maybe. Does it say we’ll wash your back if you wash ours? Perhaps. Does it say these men are careless suckers? Quite possibly. But I think, were we to do this for good Qasim, it should be with the understanding that future endeavors will not be done in the dark. The Company is not accustomed to slipping the noose around their own necks, at least, not without knowing they are doing so.”

entries.author: TheBit
entries.body: “So, which is it then, good Qasim? Do you see us as servants? Useful tools? I assure you, we can be both. But I’ll also assure you, the next task you ask of us, if there is a next task, will be one where everyone’s eyes are open. We will know what we do, and to the extent necessary why and to whom we do it. Otherwise, we have no way to know if the juice is worth the squeeze, so to speak. I do not mean to anger you, good Qasim. I just feel it is important to remind everyone that we are all earnest men, and earnest men are not to be toyed with.”

entries.author: smalls
entries.body: "I see you only as you present yourselves, Master Prancer." Qasim presses a hand against his chest. "On my honor, I have said there shall not be a third request such as these two. Might we yet negotiate some additional arrangement? Certainly, should both parties desire such. But I will not again ask you to conduct any future arrangement 'in the dark.' You have my word."

Not a war.”  He glances at Gallows.  “You’re worried about marks on the ledger? We already got one.” A small shrug. “Free barracks in a city like this don’t come clean.” His eyes shift to Prancer. “And you got your answer.” A nod toward Qasim. “No more blind work after this."  He pauses.  “So what’s left?”  He pauses.  It's annoying.  “We move a hooded man from one place to another. Night job. Quiet streets. No talking.” A faint snort. “Hell, we’ve done worse half-drunk. No contracts signed. No loyalties sworn. No names asked. We lose nothing doing it. We walk away now, we lose him.  He may not say that, but it is true, I believe.  And men like him don’t forget being turned down after they’ve opened their doors. We do it clean, we gain a place in this city before the Company even gets here.  You know, Prancer, if you had told me 25 years ago that someday I'd be standing here about to solve the world's energy problems, I would have said you're crazy. Now let's push this giant ball of oil out the window."

entries.author: smalls
entries.body:
Two wicks past evening prayer, the compound's rear gate opens without a sound. Qasim's man — compact, professional, face still as pondwater — steps forth leading a hooded man by a thin chain leash. The other end of the chain disappears beneath the hooded man's robes.

"Take this one," he says in passable Maulik, "to the Bayt al-Hikma."

At Bumble's blank stare, he continues. "The House of Wisdom. The largest building in Muirthemne. Other than the Godking's Eternal Palace."

At Bumble's still-blank, he says, "On Copper Street, where it meets the Avenue of al-Haddad."

At Bumble's yet-blank stare, he extends a finger toward a minareted skyline wreathed in stars. "You see that tower with the five points? Yes? That marks the nearest corner of the Bayt."

He hands the lead to Bumble. "In the rear of the Bayt there are three doors. The lantern over one of them will be out. That is your door. Knock twice. Give the hooded man to whoever opens the door. Leave."

entries.author: smalls
entries.body:
Bumble wordlessly sets off, the hooded man trailing equally wordlessly behind him. The hooded man slows when Bumble slows. He stops when Bumble stops. Few onlookers spare more than a glance toward Bumble and his charge. Glances can lead to trouble in Muirthemne, especially at night.

In half a wick, Bumble arrives.

The Bayt is enormous — a statement the city seems to have accepted long ago and stopped remarking upon. Marble walls the color of old bone rise four stories to a roofline of carved stone lattice, the kind of work that takes generations and assumes more will follow. The five minarets Bumble navigated by are taller still, needle-thin, each capped with a lamp that burns through the night not for prayer but for scholarship. The building occupies an entire city block and appears to be indifferent to this fact. No banners. No guards visible. Whatever this place is, it has never needed to announce itself.

Bumble makes his way across the front of the cathedral-like building and turns down an alley. Another two hundred paces puts him at the building's rear. He approaches the only door without a lit lantern and knocks. Twice.

Time passes. Bumble fidgets. The hooded man does not.

entries.author: smalls
entries.body:
Bumble begins to wonder if he was meant to literally knock twice, or knock once and then knock again. As he lifts his fist toward the door, it opens.

A Muir in dark robes stands silhouetted in the doorway, lamplight spilling around him. He steps to one side and motions for Bumble to enter.

Bumble steps into an antechamber of pale marble, cool as a cellar despite the night's heat. Across from the door he entered, five archways pierce a curved wall, each one framing a view into the library proper. What lies beyond is not easily taken in. Shelves rise from floor to ceiling — and the ceiling is very far overhead — packed with volumes of every size and color, the accumulated weight of them pressing on the air in a way that has nothing to do with smell. The stacks recede into the dimness beyond the nearest lamps, one row giving way to another and another still, until distance and shadow swallow them entirely. Somewhere in there, scholars are working. The silence is total. This is not a place where you raise your voice.

The man in dark robes raises a hand and another in similar garb appears from the rightmost archway. He accepts the leash and retraces his steps, the hooded man in tow, until both disappear beyond the arch.

The first man nods toward Bumble. "You may go."

entries.body:
**Bassam ibn Tariq, Olive Oil Merchant**

He has taken a table on the upper balcony of a restaurant whose name you will not recognize but whose prices you will. The view is the best in this quarter of the city. A boy stands behind him with a fan. There is food on the table — more than four men could finish — and he is eating without urgency, the way a man eats when he has never once wondered where the next meal was coming from.

He is broad, loud in his colors, and draped in more gold than most men will earn in a lifetime. He does not stand when you arrive.

He gestures at the food, at the chairs, at the city spread below the balcony, and then he says:

“Men think Muirthemne special for its women — eyes etched with kohl, breasts layered with golden scales, silks everywhere - 'lest a man lose his ardor along with the mystery. But I — I believe it is special for its bathhouses. Here we take mind to wash well. To present well." He eyes you impassively. "To…smell well.”

entries.author: smalls
entries.body:
He looks at the city below the balcony for a moment, then back at you, with the expression of a man who has already made his decision and is allowing you the courtesy of feeling like you made it with him.

“There is a district. Rhish blood, mostly — been there two generations, maybe three. Good people, mostly. Nervous people, currently. You understand why.”

He waves a hand.

“I walk there every month. I have done so for fifteen years. I will do so again on the morrow. I will browse the souk. I will take my tea at the Broken Minaret. I will linger and stroll and dally. And then, when I am ready, I will walk home.”

He looks at each of you in turn. “I would like you to walk with me.”

[OOC: Those with Rhish blood are nervous because the Empire of Rhi'anon (Rhish) are rumored to be marching south to invade Muirthemne. ]

entries.author: Fitz
entries.body:
Bumble listens without interrupting, eyes drifting once over the city below before settling back on Bassam.  “Men get nervous when armies start walking. Sometimes they get stupid too.”  He studies the merchant for a moment.  “You want to keep walking that district like nothing’s changed. Panic spreads faster than fire in places like this. Folks see a rich man stop showing his face, they start thinking maybe they should run too.  Do I have that about right?”

“So you walk...And we walk with you."  He pauses.  "Long as you don’t expect us to smell better by tomorrow.”

**The Walk**
Bassam moves through the quarter like a man inspecting property he already owns. He stops to inspect a bolt of cloth he won't buy, exchanges a loud word with a baker who answers him too quickly and too thinly, claps a hand on the shoulder of a man who flinches before he can stop himself. The boy with the fan trails a half-step behind, and behind him, unspoken but unmissable, four armed men in Black Company kit. Bassam doesn't introduce you. He doesn't need to. The point of you is simply that you are there, and that everyone can see you are there, and that everyone can do the arithmetic of what that means for a man who walks where he pleases with whoever he pleases at his back.

entries.author: smalls
entries.body:
The street answers him in a register just under silence. Shutters that were cracked an inch close another inch as he passes. A woman pulls a child in off a doorstep without looking at Bassam directly, the way you avoid looking at the sun. An old man seated outside a shuttered shopfront watches the whole procession go by with an expression that has nothing soft left in it — not fear, not quite, but its older and more tired cousin. Twice you catch a man's eyes on Bassam's back after he's passed, the look gone flat and hard the moment Bassam might have turned around, gone again by the time he actually does.

At the souk he takes his time, fingering silks and haggling half-heartedly over almonds he doesn't need, and the merchants serve him with the particular speed of men who want this transaction finished and this customer elsewhere. One young man near the spice stalls says something low to his neighbor — not loud enough to catch, but the neighbor's eyes flick to your party and back, and the young man doesn't say anything else for the rest of the walk. At the Broken Minaret he takes his tea on a low wall in full view of the lane, in no hurry at all, and for those ten minutes the entire street seems to perform the business of not watching him.

entries.author: smalls
entries.body: Nobody raises a hand. Nobody raises a voice above what's needed to sell him dates. But the quarter knows exactly what it's looking at — a fat man in gold, untouched and untouchable, walking his own street with the Black Company carrying his confidence for him — and the quarter hates it quietly, the way people hate things they can't yet afford to hate out loud.

entries.author: smalls
entries.body: OOC: So, in effect, this was a bit of a performative walk for Bassam - showing the Rhish distrcit that he's unafraid, despite the impending war, and that his power still holds. Those of you that accompanised him were a visible token of that power and, perhaps, indicate that the Black is allied (or at least connected) with Bassam himself.

entries.author: smalls
entries.body: OOC: You've done the three things he asked.  Deliver an unopened message, escort a hooded dude, and stroll through the Rhish district of Muirthemne. In return, you have a barracks for the Company's arrival and Bassam takes you to a different quarter of the city.

entries.author: smalls
entries.body:
Past the souk, he turns down a lane none of you would have found on your own and stops at the foot of a narrow bridge over a canal gone green with algae. He clasps his hands behind his back.
"This is the last of what I'll ask of you," he says, not quite meeting anyone's eyes. "There's a woman. Across the water. She asked for you — by name, or near enough — which is more than she's done for any man I've brought here in fifteen years." He pauses. "I don't know what she'll say. I don't know that it'll mean anything. But she asked, and I am not in the habit of refusing women who are usually right."
He does not cross the bridge himself.
Across the canal, a woman sits with her back against the wall of the souk, feet dangling above the water. She is not restrained. She has never needed to be. She watches you cross with the patient attention of someone who has been waiting longer than the walk took.
She speaks before any of you can.

entries.author: smalls
entries.body: ***"I was right. Tonk! The goat loves not the cares of the serpent, the serpent cares not for the loves of the goat. Tonk! The deck is stronger than any hand — do not play against the deck. Go to the goats. Go up to them. Tonk! She bit me did you know bit me she did. Tonk! One you have not met, nor his works. His works will find you before ever he does. Catch him red-handed! Tonk! The moon was small and red and red and small was the moon. Tonk! Books are memories. Your book remembers. All books do. His book, too — read between the lines! The goats again and again the goats. Tonk! I was right."***

entries.author: smalls
entries.body:
She says nothing further. She returns her attention to the water, feet still swinging, as if you had already left.
Bassam is waiting at the foot of the bridge when you return, hands still clasped behind his back. He does not ask what she said. "Well," he says, and for once there is nothing performed in it. "I expect you'll want to return to your barracks now." He turns to go, then pauses. "She's never been wrong. I want that on the record, for whatever it's worth to men like you."

entries.author: The_Frostrune
entries.body: “Master Bassam, you said this woman clearly asked for us.  How did you know?  By what name did she call us?”

entries.author: The_Frostrune
entries.body:
Assume a couple of days have passed since the pitched battle outside the walls of <insert name>.  Gallows wants to visit Tadpole

Gallows respectfully knocks on door to Tadpole’s room, “Hey Tadpole, you in there?”

The paper thin walls fail to mask his exasperated groan before the “Sure.  C’mon in.”

Gallows cracks the door to see if anyone else is inside before entering.  Tadpole hardly looks up from the book he is reading at his makeshift desk, “I told you yesterday, I will not discuss anything the Captain said….”

“I know. I know,”, Gallows cuts in.  “I’m not here for that… exactly.”

Tadpole finally looks up.  “Go on…”, he responds hesitantly, a curious sparkle returning to his eye.  

“You know something big is going on; something fucking weird and magical.  Did the Captain send you, and us, to Telembor to look for that book and the lost remnant of the Black?  Did he know it was there?”

“DAMMIT GALLOWS!”, the normally jovial mage explodes, “I told you my discussions with the Old Man are off limits.  Now get out of here!”

Gallows holds up his hands in surrender, “Sorry.  Sorry.  Look, this is all fucked!  You gotta have some idea of what is going on here.  You saw them dead brothers rise.  You were scared shitless of whatever was trapped beyond that seal.  We now have a book we can’t read until we get to the same spot where the entry was written.  We went through trials at Scholomance put to us by three talking heads!  Yeah… just heads.  Mounted on silver pipes.  And carried around by dark robed silent monks.  Fucked up, right?  And that’s just the start of it!”

entries.author: The_Frostrune
entries.body:
“The unlocked book now takes us on the reverse journey of those Brothers entombed at the Telembor.  We find the hand of the Collector, which leads us to the head of the Collector… which of course is somehow still alive and able to talk!  Did you know he was supposed to be the 4th head with those Scholomance freaks?  Which took us to Strand which brought us to here.  Along the way we get attacked by Black warships with Red sails that are shutting down all the coastal shipping by driving crews insane with some sirens call.  People are bleeding out their ears and their eyes roll up white.  They go all catatonic until something triggers them, then they turn into raving lunatics and scream until their throats pop, yeah.. pop.  Its gross.  No saving them.  Then we roll in here for a happy reunion and we are besieged by an army of stitched together dead men lead by an equally dead Lord with an obviously broken neck.  Lastly, for the cherry on top of this shit sundae, the Captain signs a deal with the 8’ tall freak show that caused the damn siege in the first place!”

“What thee FUCK Tadpole?!  What the fuck is going on?  None of this is natural.  I can kill Mir, and Rhish, and sand nomads; its what a soldier does.  Not werewolves, dead men, and 20’ tall statues with great tits.  I’d be thrown in the stocks as the town fool if I told these stories anywhere else.”

Gallows sags.  He seems exhausted, his eyes wild.  “What are these beings?  The Collector, Soulblighter, The Sleeper, the floating cold-as-death witch you all encountered crossing the mountains?  What are we dealing with?  These ain’t no normal contracts and these ain’t no normal times.”

entries.author: TheBit
entries.body:
Prancer walks into the room clearly upset. "Tadpole, we need to talk about The Captain and this book. I..."

Noticing the expressions on Gallow's and Tadpole's faces, he stops mid sentence. ” Okay, okay. I can read a room.”

Prancer turns on one foot and walks back out of the room.

entries.author: smalls
entries.title: Session 2 · The reckoning
entries.label: Session recap
entries.description: From the Rhish ambush and the Inaccessible Collection to the Collector’s Vault, Harran, and a new contract with Soulblighter.

blocks.text: I wasn't there for most of this.

runs.text: I wasn't there for most of this.

blocks.text: I want that said plainly before anything else, because the Annals are supposed to be truth and I won't pretend to a closeness I didn't have. What follows came to me in pieces — in the queue for the surgeon's tent at Harran, during our two-week march on the coastal road, or fireside at night. They answered, some of them freely, some of them like men paying off a debt they hadn't agreed to. Where two Brothers told it two ways, I've picked the way that fit best with what I saw of them after. Where nobody would tell it at all, I've said so, and left the hole where the hole was.

The Rhish column came apart from the ass-end forward. Bumble put it in Bumbletalk: "LT said get their attention. We did. Pourin’ oil on them sunstroke rickeys and then lighting those boys on fire tends to do that.”  While that’s harsh work, no way to coat it otherwise, it was needed; I was in the head of that ambush and the LT was about two minutes from having the horn blow the retreat. A near run thing, it was.

blocks.text: Afterward, we marched into the city feeling like we had made chicken salad out of chickenshit. Five hundred of us had wrecked an entire column, and delayed the main vanguard. This, despite the fact we had been ordered to hold a collection of mudbrick walls that – more Bumbletalk here – “a midget with a huge dangling dick coulda stepped over.” Muirthemne’s been around a while and it’s gotten pretty good, I reckon, on placing the blame anywhere other than on their precious Godking’s shoulders. A group of ugly, pale-faced foreign mercenaries who “abandoned their post” served nicely enough. I knew the Old Man was measuring the end of that Muirthemne contract the moment he saw the first sullen stare upon our return. Bigby departed for the West with his Fist within two days.

blocks.text: There’s a name that’s going to be forgotten in all of this, and that name is Umar al-Khatib, and in some ways I figure he started everything that was about to happen. Like most Muirthemne minor nobles, Umar was caught up in the cogs of the Godking’s Court. He was sent out on garrison duty and was relieved by the Company. The fact the Court ordered his relief doesn’t, apparently, excuse him for the fact he and his men returned to the city before the whole north fell to the Rhish.

blocks.text: The Day of Reckoning, they called it. The Godking fingered eight nobles who “failed to defend the City” and sent out twice as many hit squads to even the score. Killing a general or two, as they say, tends to stiffen the resolve of the rest of them. Our man Umar was marked for death. Probably would have happened except, I hear it said, ol’ Umar owed our patron Bassam quite o’ bit of the yellow stuff. Drains took a knuckle out to find him and bring him back, and the devil’s knuckle was ordered to be on overwatch. The lads posted up on a dry aqueduct and waited. Two things happened at damned near the same time – the knuckle spotted two hit squads converging on Umar while shouts and steel sounded from down the Veiled Boulevard. Guess there was a decision made that getting Umar was the right play, and Drains and his boys could fend for themselves. Rough arithmetic, that. But it worked. And where’s why I say Umar started everything that follows: he has a nephew, and that nephew works in the City’s great library, and Umar now owed the knuckle a favor.

I asked Prancer what they learned in that library and he simply said: “Scholomance.” Prancer can be a right ass when he wants to.

blocks.text: A little further south the knuckle hired a Myrish huntsman in a shithole named Thume. He guided them into Forest Heart before skedaddling. Knuckle says they followed an old road for days and days, until it deposited them at the base of a monument.  On that obelisk of stone, so they claim, were the names of ten fallen Brothers – men back from that ancient company that walked alongside the writer of their swirly-words Annals. Brothers dead so long their names had worn off the stone along with the weather. Tulip mentioned it only once, quietly: "Somebody ought to remember they was Brothers, like us. Now all in the mud."

Pussy says Twitch got turned around a few times, but Twitch swears he knew the path from start to finish. I believe Pussy.

blocks.text: Then it was off to the port o’ Tince with a living head in a burlap sack. Tince smelled of empty harbor and idle men long before anyone said a word about ships not coming. A Myr ship’s captain named Jetu Balkh took them out anyway, and two days into open water they found the Harrow's Wake adrift with a crew that had gone somewhere between living and not, ears bleeding, faces slack. Towed her home. The bells woke the crew up wrong, and they came up swinging and biting and tearing at whatever was nearest, and the knuckle simply cut the tow lines and let the half-dead finish their own argument. The Fishwives held their bargain after. Pussy, who says perhaps six words a week and makes each one count, allowed: "Didn't need us for that part. Just needed us to let it happen."

blocks.text: They were there with Bigby and the Harran defenders for three weeks before we arrived with the full company. entries.body: "Hold up," Tadpole raises a hand to Prancer. "You need to hear this." The chubby wizard stands and pulls the tent flap closed. His voice is soft when he speaks. "I ain't gonna talk about the Captain and Telembor. And I don't know much more than you lads do about all these other...things. But," he says, eyes twinkling, "I'm not sure we're not doing exactly what we ought. Exactly what them ancient Brothers *wanted * us to do.  I mean - the breadcrumbs are laid out pretty damned conveniently, no? You got the Book which led to Scholomance which led to the Hand which led to the Head. I'm thinking these, ah, things could *help* us. And maybe the Captain knows that, too."

And their running probably put some of us in the mud that weren’t otherwise headin’ there, leastwise not today.

That head, sitting on the mud, just yammering away – running us a blue streak up and down – until it weren’t.

entries.author: The_Frostrune
entries.body: Gallows wrinkles up his face and scratches his beard, “How do you see that?  Seems to me we’re undoing what them brothers did, maybe even putting that Collector fuck back together!”

entries.author: smalls
entries.body: Tadpole opens his mouth to respond, thinks a moment, closes it, then opens it again. "You got me there, Gal." He shrugs.

entries.author: TheBit
entries.body:
Prancer sits down at Tadpole’s workbench and quietly stares at the candles that serve to provide the meager light by which he works. He sits there, motionless, long enough that it starts to become uncomfortable. Finally, Tadpole breaks the silence. 

“Prancer?”

Prancer doesn’t budge initially, but just as Gallows starts to clear his throat as if to speak, Prancer’s head dips a bit then he turns in the chair to face them.

Prancer admits in a voice not far above a whisper “I don’t know. I don’t know and that is what eats at me. Let me be clear. I have never made it a habit to question the orders of our leaders. I know The Black requires that. Without orders and men willing to follow them, The Company does not exist, at least, not for long.”

“If this were a simple matter of me wrestling with whether The Black chose the wrong patron in some meaningless conflict, I would have brushed it off without a second thought. I have done this many times in the past. As far as I am concerned, I square up with The Company every month when they hand me my coin.”

“But can we all agree that the stakes seem quite a bit higher here? Ever since we arrived here on this side of the Steppes, things have been sideways.” Prancer looks to Tadpole and Gallows in turn. He sees neither confirmation nor dissent. He sighs. “I can only describe it as, and forgive me because I would ordinarily choose much more perfumed words, some crazy fucking shit.”

“I believe now that The Captain knew full well what he was doing when he dragged us across those Steppes. I am not sure how he knew, or how much he knew, but I have no doubt he knew something. I wonder though if he expected all that we have seen. A part of me hopes so, because that reassures me that things are going to plan.”

entries.author: TheBit
entries.body:
He looks at Tadpole, then to Gallows. “I am going to go along to get along. I am going to try and convince myself that we are doing exactly what the Annalist in this book intended when he penned it ages ago. I am going to continue to believe, since he has never steered us horribly wrong before, that The Captain knows what he is doing. I am going to choose to believe these things, despite what my gut tells me. But there will come a time when I will need this to make more sense, especially if things continue to get more and more fucked up.”

Prancer nods curtly, and walks out of the room

entries.author: The_Frostrune
entries.body:
Gallows sighs, “That fool really needs to understand the meaning of inner monologue.”

“…but he’s not wrong”, interjects Tadpole.

“Of course he’s not wrong!”, Gallows snaps.  “Half the company is probably thinking something similar.  Giving voice to it is dangerous however.  By the love of stone and stream , I hope the Old Man puts some clarity to this soon.  Sorry for pushing on ya Tadpole but this is driving me nuts.”

entries.author: Kartoonstew
entries.body: Tulip nods in agreement. “Yup”

entries.author: smalls
entries.body:
Prancer returns to the tent moments after departing, an odd "got caught with my hand in the cookie jar" look on his face. And, right on his heels, comes the Old Man himself and the Annalist Croaker. 
Gallows and Tadpole jump to their feet, but the Captain waves them to sit down. "We're mercenaries, not military."  Seeing Prancer standing aimlessly, the Captain waves him to a camp stool. “Sit, Prancer.” 
Prancer sits. Quickly.
The Old Man settles onto Tadpole’s trunk and Croaker, with a last look outside, closes the flap and crosses his arms.
There’s a moment of awkward silence as the Captain looks at everyone and no one looks at the Captain. “Evening, men,” he says. “You got the book on you, Prancer?”
Prancer pats his satchel. “Yes, sir.”
“And the Head?”
Prancer pats another satchel. “Yes, sir.”
The Captain nods. “Can’t remember if you boys asked me to track down the bread crumbs that book was laying, or whether I asked you to do it. But you did it, and you did it well. Thank you for that.”
Prancer opens his mouth, closes it, opens it again, and then Gallows replies, “You’re welcome, sir.”
“You found those things fair and square and you paid blood to do it. So what I’m about to say is a request, not an order. It’s important you know that.  And if you need to talk to the other lads in the knuckle that likewise bled, well, that’s fine too.”
“What can we do for you, Cap?” Prancer says after a moment.
“I would like you to give the Head to Tadpole.”
“Tadpole?” Prancer asks, confused.
“Tadpole?” Gallows asks, confused.
“Me?” Tadpole asks, confused.
“Yes,” the Captain answers.
Brothers aren’t in the habit of asking the Old Man why, but three voices say, “Why?” in unison.

entries.author: smalls
entries.body:
“Two reasons.” The Captain holds up a finger. “First, the best person in this outfit to study that…thing…is Tadpole. No one else knows which way is up when it comes to weird shit like an old Head that ain’t dead yet.”
“S-study it?” Tadpole stammers, his face shining with both trepidation and enthusiasm.
“Talk to it. Learn what it knows.”
“Sir,” Gallows says, frowning, “should we be having this conversation while the Head is, ah, um, right here with us?”
The Captain leans back. “Maybe not, but it’s out there now all the same.”
“You said there were two reasons,” Prancer says, eyes thoughtful.
“Right. Second, I would prefer not to have the Head be anywhere near our…patron. You boys are doubtless gonna be close to him, time to time, but we can make Tadpole scarce.”
“I’ll do it,” Tadpole announces, slapping his stump on his ample belly.
“Ain’t your decision to make,” Croaker speaks for the first time. “It’s theirs.”
The Old Man nods. “Right.” He fixes his gaze on Prancer and Gallows. “Got an answer, or wanna talk with your boys? Whatever you decide, that’ll be the end of it.”

entries.author: The_Frostrune
entries.body: "What do you want done with the hand?", Gallows adds.  "I still got that thing but it ain't moved nor twitched in a bunch of weeks."

entries.author: smalls
entries.body: The Captain shares a look with Croaker then turns to you and shrugs. "I've got half a mind to burn it. From what you told me the Hand served its purpose and opened the door to the Collector's Vault. And that Vault is nothing more than a pile of rubble, now." He frowns. "Then again, them old Brothers buried it for a reason. Maybe let Tadpole see what he can learn before making a choice we can't undo.  Your call."

entries.author: The_Frostrune
entries.body:
“I’d be happy to be rid of it either way, but we’ll see what the rest of the boys say,” Gallows replies.

Gallows shares a sidelong look with Prancer then looks directly at the Captain.  There is a visible, sheepish hesitation; a few seconds of war behind his eyes that eventually comes to a conclusion.  He takes a deep breath and squares up knowing his time might now be measured in seconds, “Sir.  At the risk of the lash… or worse, I owe you the truth.  I was in here putting Tadpole to the question.  Questions about talking heads and zombie armies and creatures that just go by titles like they was some darkling Gods: Soulblighter, The Collector, The Sleeper, Shiver.  The Black of old, them that wrote this book, they knew something.  They FOUGHT these creatures.  Yet we just bled against… then took service with one!”  That last bit came out as a hiss between gritted teeth.

Gallows quickly regains his composure, “I know enough to know I ain’t as smart you, or the LT, or any of the other officers.  I have always trusted the chain of command, always followed orders.  But Sir,” <a little quiver to the voice?> another steadying breath, “you shook me the other day; rocked me to my core.  I love the Black.  I wake up everyday knowing I’m going to die for the Black.”

Again a pause.  “I’m scared.  I’m confused.  I’m hurt.  I’m trying to make it make sense.  You don’t owe it to me.  You don’t owe it to any of us.  But please tell me there’s a reason.”

Well, there it is.  He knows he just crossed a line.  Better him than Prancer.  Even for all his annoying faggotry, its plain to see he’s destined to be an officer someday.  Gallows blinks slowly and goes rigid.  He is ready to take a punch in the face or the call to Mercy to get dragged out to the whipping post…. or the gallows.  He smirks inwardly at the irony.

entries.author: TheBit
entries.body: Prancer sits quietly for once. He stares downward seemingly fixated on the cuticle of his left thumb. He pulls out a dart and starts meticulously tending to it. His gaze doesn't stray from his hand.

entries.author: smalls
entries.body:
The Captain eyes Gallows for a lingering moment before turning to Croaker. "What do you think? The coin?"
Croaker looks between the two of them. "I do, sir."
The Old Man reaches into his coat and comes out with a single coin between two fingers, setting it down on the trunk between himself and Gallows with a small, deliberate click. Just an ordinary piece — worn smooth at the edges, some old profile stamped on one face gone soft with handling.
"You look at me and see your Captain. Some old salt counting away the years and putting quill to parchment so Gramps can buy the necessaries." He smiles, soft, taking the edge off it. "Once, though, I was just a Brother in a knuckle. Spent what I made and borrowed what I didn't. Gramps used to run me out of the Commissary. Didn't need no horn in his ear to hear back then."
It's rare for him to talk about the time before he was Captain. Rare for him to talk this much at all. For a stretch the only sound is the camp outside — laughter, murmuring, the ordinary noise of an evening that has nothing to do with this tent.
"Once me and my knuckle lads — they're all in the mud now — got a rare side contract." His face darkens, eyes seeing something that isn't in the tent. "Easy duty. Boring duty. Guard some nobleman called Greenfingers."
"The Gardener, sir," Croaker says, quiet.

entries.author: smalls
entries.body:
"Right. The Gardener." He stares at the coin a moment before going on. "Had a big garden inside his high walls. Weren't no real garden. He had about forty women in there with him. Some pretty as all get out, some plain, some downright homely. Heavy ones, light as a feather, dark and fair." He smiles, and it's a sad thing. "One I remember. She'd come to the gate time to time, where we stood duty, and if you so much as looked at her — well, she'd blush red as a holiday apple."
His gaze settles on Gallows. Waits just long enough that Prancer makes the mistake of glancing up — and gets the same look turned on him a moment, before it comes back to Gallows.
"Only thing those women had in common was that they had half-legs and half-arms." He puts his hands on his thighs. "Aye. Lopped off at the elbow." A chopping motion. "Lopped off at the knee."
Croaker doesn't move. He's heard this one before.
"The Gardener called them his pets. Never seen a zoo myself, but somebody told me that word once and I guess that's what he figured he had. Them women, all of them, crawling around on stumps like goats or dogs or what-not."
He taps the coin. "Go on. Ask it."

entries.author: smalls
entries.body:
Gallows doesn't move. "Ask it what, sir?"
"Whatever you were fixing to ask me. Ask the coin instead. Ask it why we — you, me, our Brothers — killed every man, woman, and child in Cascera after the sack. Ask it about the Gardener." He nudges the coin half an inch toward Gallows, patient, a man laying out a hand of cards he already knows the value of. "And while you're at it, ask it what it thinks about Soulblighter, seeing as how there's about to be a great deal more of its cousins coming out of that particular pocket. Go on, now. I'll wait."
Gallows looks between the Captain and the coin, jaw tight, trying to decide if this is mockery. The Captain's face gives him nothing either way. Not amused. Not stern. Just watching.
"It ain't gonna answer, sir."
"No," he agrees. "It ain't. Not if you ask it nice, not if you ask it with a blade to it, not if you melt it down and ask the piss-colored puddle. Thirty years I've been asking coins questions and I got thirty years of silence to show for it."
He picks it back up, turns it once between his fingers. The profile catches the lamplight and loses it again.
"That's the trick of the whole business, and it ain't a trick anybody plays on you — you play it on yourself, every time, because the alternative's worse. You want the coin to have took a side. Weighed the Gardener's women, weighed Cascera, weighed whatever's coming with this Soulblighter business, and come down somewhere. Good or bad, don't matter, long as it's somewhere. Man can live with a coin that's wicked. Man's got a harder time living with a coin that just don't care."
He sets it down again, in front of himself this time, two fingers pinning it to the wood.

entries.author: smalls
entries.body:
"But that's all it is. It don't care. Never has. It'll buy you bread same as it'll buy you a knife in a man's back, and it won't lose a wink of sleep either way — on account of it don't sleep, on account of it ain't alive, on account of the only thing in this whole arrangement that's alive and has to carry the weight of it is you." He taps it twice. "Not this. You."
He pockets it, the small motion final as a door closing.
"What we just done here is what Croaker and I have learned to call the coin answer. You're a sharp lad, Gallows. This ain't the first time, and won't be the last, some Brother's come to me asking the why's and wherefore's of a contract I signed."
Croaker nods, saying nothing.
"When I asked them kind of questions of my own Captain, back in my youth — off that same stretch of sentry duty at the Gardener's gate — I got a different answer. A fist to the face and a spell tied to the lashing pole. Different times, them."
He gets to his feet. The others rise with him.
"Both them answers are shit. But the coin never lied to you. That's the best you'll get out of this outfit, and it's the only one worth trusting."

entries.author: smalls
entries.body:
Croaker holds up a black robe and the Captain shrugs his arms through it.
"Gallows. And Prancer." He looks between them. "Tell Mercy the two of you have latrine digging duty for the next tenday. You two and none others. He won't ask why. Doubtless some of the other lads will thank you for it."
He ducks through the flap without another word. Croaker gathers the lamp, and for a moment the tent is darker than it was — just Gallows, Prancer, and the shape of a coin that isn't there anymore, pressed into the grain of the trunk where it sat.

entries.author: TheBit
entries.body:
Prancer slaps his thigh and stands wearing a wan smile. "Whelp, you really stepped in it, Gallows."

Every muscle in Gallows' body tenses as his head snaps in Prancer's direction and glowers at him. If looks could kill, Prancer would be a thin red paste. 

The glib smile on Prancer's face melts away instantly and is replaced with nervous unease. "Sorry. I'll uh...I'm going to go change my clothes." As he walks past Gallows toward the door, he raises his hand, pauses with uncertainty, then lightly claps Gallows on the back.

Just as Prancer is about to pass through the threshold, Gallows barks "Prancer!"

Prancer stops dead in his tracks and turns to look back. 

Gallows raises his head and stares daggers at his Brother. ”I get the good shovel."

Prancer nods slowly. ”Of course, Gallows. Of course."

entries.author: The_Frostrune
entries.body: After Prancer leaves, Gallows sits quietly for another few seconds seemingly oblivious he's in Tadpole's tent.  His shoulders sag, his head in his hands.  He is the very image of a defeated man.... then he laughs.  Just a low throaty chuckle but it is wholly out of place; almost insane.  And then he does the thing that you have all caught at various different times, he looks over his shoulder into the shadows of an empty corner and speaks, "You enjoy this don't you?  I suppose it is pretty funny.  If you can't take me yet, you can watch me wish for it.  Well... fuck you.  I still ain't ready."

entries.author: The_Frostrune
entries.body: He stands to leave and is suddenly aware of Tadpole just looking at him curiously.  He just returns the look, shrugs, and walks out.  No sense in waiting, time to find Mercy.

blocks.text: You throw open your tent flap and step into air that has weight to it — nothing like the dry furnace-breath of the Maul, where the heat used to flay a man's throat raw before noon. You spent damned near a year cursing the heat; you're now learning how to curse the water.

entries.author: The_Frostrune
entries.body:
Since that night in Tadpole’s tent shortly after the siege, Gallows has been quieter, more isolated.  A learned man might say introspective.  He paid the price busting his ass in the ditches with Prancer without complaint.  Oddly both of them did.  Neither spoke another word about it.  Didn’t need to.    They were both hopelessly intoxicated by the mystery but too loyal to give it further voice.  Questions would only hurt the Black.  Neither wanted that.  As his wounds recovered he took to the solace of a terrain he was much more familiar with, setting snares for rabbits and fishing the creeks.  Only the knuckle really noticed the change.  No one gave it voice.  

A little spark came back sometime that evening, after the last reading by Croaker and the very limited open acknowledgement of the Taken by the Captain.  Sitting arounds the small cookfire he approached Prancer once again, not loudly but not exactly hidden either.

“Hey Prancer, crack the book.  Read that passage again; the one after the monument had been raised, where they talk about chopping up The Collector.”

Prancer gives him an odd look but decides to indulge him.  He shrugs and pulls the ancient volume from the protective satchel and thumbs through the few legible pages until he finds the one Gallows mentioned.  As he begins to read, a few of the others gather closer to hear.

entries.author: The_Frostrune
entries.body:
*“Always feel like I need to apologize when I go a turn without writing down much.” 

“Ain’t no reason for it. None of them lads here read what I write. Pennick says “if only” are the two saddest words and “I remember” only a jot less so, so he don’t wanna take no gander. But in the heyday, lads, when just about every night someone’d jump atop a wagon and do some reading, well, they was nice nights. Made a man want to pen stuff down. 
Not tossing excuses but what with the scrap that sent Barrow and good men to the mud, and what with the sounds the forest makes at night, writing ain’t been easy for a spell. Not leastwise since we raised the monument to our fallen – them stacked stones surrounded by silent trees and a screaming forest.”*

entries.author: The_Frostrune
entries.body:
He continues through the passage with the somber pace and timber of priest, giving proper homage to the long ago Brother who penned it.

*“… But Cabbage said no. And Cabbage’s face showed he remembered **what that head had done at Gregor’s Ditch**, back when that head still had a body. And Cymbals – Cymbals who ain’t never heard someone tell him no and not bitch up a storm about it – just nodded. Cymbals is ornery but Cymbals ain’t dumb.”*

Prancer’s eyes flickered up to meet Gallows.  Just for a second but he caught the tight-lipped nod.

*“The Hand got us through. Sapling said it would. And I ain’t throwin’ no shade at Sapling, mind you, but we ain’t used to a plan working as a plan ought. I remember how we got that Hand, when we finally** run the Collector to ground**, way down at the world’s toe at Harran. Carved him up. Head off first, ‘course. Then one hand, then the other. A foot. Then the boys got creative – ‘**specially them boys what were in the thick o’ it at Gregor’s** – and it was tough to watch but tougher to realize you enjoyed watching it. The Collector squirmed and kicked through it all. Hands crawling around like two sunstroke crabs. That head, sitting on the mud, just yammering away – running us a blue streak up and down – until it weren’t.”*

entries.author: The_Frostrune
entries.body: Prancer finished the passage and closed the book.  The audible thump seemed to break the spell and everyone went back to back to whatever they were doing, everyone except Gallows.  He took a long pull on the bottle of brandy he had dragged all the way from Muirethemne and passed it appreciatively to Prancer.  He heard what he wanted to hear.  Our next stop, Gregor’s Ditch, was also in the book.  The Collector had done some shit there.  Confirmation we are still on the trail.
